```
the system must be independent of the agents used to build it, so the data can be
updated later or rebuilt on another computer without any LLM.

(discovery + download + checksum manifest) rather than files alone; treat files without a
reproducing script as incomplete. Prefer polite sequential fetching with pauses.
```

```
# Visual direction: the shipping ledger

The dashboard reads like a printed price sheet or a merchant's ledger, not like
a SaaS dashboard. Warm paper, black ink, hairline rules, figures set in a
newspaper serif, and colour reserved for meaning.

## Why it fits

The user is a shop owner deciding where a few dollars per parcel go. The
decision lives in a handful of numbers: which carrier is cheapest, what one
parcel costs, whether the flat price still leaves a margin. A ledger puts those
numbers first, in the largest type on the page, and pushes everything else
(assumptions, sliders, provenance) into small, quiet type around them. Rules
and columns instead of cards make it feel like an account the owner keeps, and
they print well for an accountant.

## Hierarchy

1. **The answer** (cheapest carrier, cost per parcel, margin): display serif,
   `--text-figure`, tabular figures, carrier or money colour.
2. **The question** each section answers: display serif, `--text-xl`.
3. **The owner's parcel set**: once loaded, a one-line strip (count, share to
   homes, speed split) with the full summary behind "Details", so the
   questions and the answer stay above the fold, also on a phone.

### Rule for every question view (issues #5 and #6)

The answer is the largest element of its section. Put it first under the
question, in `.answer > .answer__figure` (`--text-figure`), with a short
`.answer__caption` saying what it is ("UPS Ground, $8.41 per parcel, $1.58
margin"). Nothing else in the section, including the question (`--text-xl`),
chart titles and table figures, may be set larger. Charts and tables come
after the answer and explain it.
4. **Assumptions** (year, rate card, fuel, peak, flat price): a left rail in the
   UI face at `--text-sm`, always visible on desktop, a bottom sheet on phones
   behind a one-line summary bar.

## Palette (`src/styles/tokens.css`)

| Token | Light | Dark | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--paper` | `#F5F1E8` | `#15140F` | page |
| `--sheet` | `#FBF9F4` | `#1E1C17` | rail, inputs, raised panels |
| `--ink` | `#1C1B18` | `#EDE8DC` | text, rules, focus ring |
| `--ink-muted` | `#5E5A50` | `#A9A292` | secondary text (6.1:1 / 7.3:1) |
| `--carrier-usps` | `#1F4E9A` | `#7FA8EE` | USPS everywhere (7.1:1 / 7.7:1) |
| `--carrier-ups` | `#7A4E0F` | `#D9A35A` | UPS everywhere (6.4:1 / 8.2:1) |
| `--carrier-fedex` | `#9C2A7E` | `#E68AC9` | FedEx everywhere (6.1:1 / 7.8:1) |
| `--loss` | `#B3261E` | `#F2877E` | negative margin (5.8:1 / 7.5:1) |
| `--profit` | `#1D6B3F` | `#6FCB94` | positive margin (5.8:1 / 9.4:1) |
| `--mock` | `#8A5A00` | `#E8B860` | the mock-data banner only |

Contrast ratios are against `--paper` and meet WCAG AA for body text in both
themes. Carrier hues follow the brands loosely (postal blue, brown, purple)
so the owner recognises them without a legend. Blue and purple are close for
some colour-vision deficiencies, so colour is never the only cue: every
carrier mark carries its name or initial, and money always carries a sign and
the word "loss" or "margin".

Each carrier also has a `-wash` tint for backgrounds and heatmap cells
(issue #5 scales intensity between the wash and the full colour).

## Type

- **Newsreader** (display serif, optical sizes) for questions and figures.
  A newspaper face gives the editorial voice and has good tabular numerals.
- **IBM Plex Sans** for the interface: labels, controls, tables. Industrial,
  slightly technical, legible at 12-14 px.

Both load from Google Fonts with `display=swap`; fallbacks are Georgia and
Helvetica/Arial. All figures use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` so
columns of prices line up.

## Spacing and shape

A 4 px base (`--space-1` … `--space-8`: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 72 px) with a
deliberate jump to 48-72 px between sections, so sections read as chapters.
Corners are nearly square (`--radius: 2px`). Separation comes from hairline
rules (`--rule`) and one heavy rule under the masthead and active tab, not
from shadows; the only shadow is on the mobile controls sheet, which really
does sit above the page.

## Motion

Only opacity and transform, 120-220 ms, for the sheet and tab underline. All
of it is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.

## Charts (for issues #5 and #6)

- Use the carrier tokens for series and cells; read them in JS with
  `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue("--carrier-usps")`
  or the `carrierColor()` helper in `src/lib/carriers.ts`, so dark mode works.
- Axis text in `--ink-muted`, gridlines in `--rule`, no chart borders.
- Announced increases and projections are dashed lines in the carrier colour.

## Questions 3 and 4 (issue #6)

Code: `src/views/blended/` (Q3) and `src/views/yearly/` (Q4). The pieces every
view shares live in one place: formatting and margin wording in `src/lib/format.ts`,
carrier names, colours and years in `src/lib/carriers.ts`, hooks (`useDebounced`,
`useLastData`, `useCssColors`) in `src/hooks/`, UI (`ChartFrame`, `ChipGroup`,
`NeedParcels`, `LoadProblem`) in `src/components/`, and their CSS in
`src/styles/views.css`, `chips.css` and `chart.css`.

**Q3, blended cost.** Answer first: the cheapest single carrier and its blended
cost per parcel (`--text-figure`), the others with their gap, then the
"best mix" (cheapest carrier per parcel) and its saving. Directly under it, the
verdict box answers "does my shipping price cover the cost?" in the money
colour (`--loss` or `--profit` border and wash), `--text-2xl`, with the share of
parcels shipped at a loss and a margin table per carrier (signed amount plus
the word "loss" or "margin", and a loss-share meter). Then the segment chips
(radio-like toggle buttons, 44 px tall, a check mark on the selected one so the
state is not colour alone), which re-query `/api/blended` and repeat the
segment's result next to the parcel count, because the answer above may be off
screen. Then the stacked cost split.

- Cost split colours (tokens in `src/styles/tokens.css`): neutral `--q3-base` for the
  base rate, a single teal ramp `--q3-sur-1..4` for surcharge kinds (darkest =
  largest kind; beyond three kinds they fold into "Other surcharges"), and
  `--q3-fuel` (ink) for fuel. Teal sits outside the carrier and money hues.
  Each carrier's row label carries its name, total and surcharge/fuel shares,
  so the split reads without the legend.

**Q4, year over year.** Answer first: for the carrier cheapest in the latest
year every carrier publishes, the percent change from its first year, with the
dollars and the announced increases compounded over the same years. A
next-year slider (default: that carrier's latest announced increase) sits in a
raised `--sheet` panel with the projected cost. The line chart uses solid
carrier lines with a marker shape per carrier (USPS circle, UPS square, FedEx
triangle; blue and purple are close under protanopia, see the validator note
below), dashed lines for the announced-increase path and dotted segments for
the projection. A "Scale" toggle switches to an index (each carrier's first
year = 100, announced paths and projection indexed the same way); it is the
default on phones, where the dollar gap between USPS and the others flattens
the slopes. Points with a note carry a "!" badge; the notes are listed in
plain words under the chart. "How much of the change is fuel?" sits right
under the chart with a small per-year fuel table. The driver chart is a
diverging bar chart from zero: warm `--q4-up` when a segment made parcels
dearer, cool `--q4-down` when cheaper (neither is the loss/profit pair), sorted
by size. Each row label gives both the contribution to the total (what the
bars show, they add up to the change) and the change per parcel within the
segment ("each", `change_total / parcels`), so a small segment that rose fast
is not hidden by a big one; the sentence names the largest contributor and,
when different, the fastest-rising segment.

**Accessibility.** Every chart is a `<figure>` with a visible text summary as
its caption and a "Show as table" toggle (`aria-pressed`). The chart SVG is
`aria-hidden`; the summary and the table carry the content. Carrier colour is
never alone: names, marker shapes or row labels go with it.

**Colour check.** The dataviz palette validator flags the carrier trio as below
the CVD target (USPS/FedEx ΔE about 5 under protanopia, light and dark), which
DESIGN.md already anticipated; Q3/Q4 therefore always pair carrier colour with
the carrier name or a marker shape.

## Q1 quote and Q2 breakeven views (issue #5)

Code in `src/views/QuoteView.tsx`, `src/views/BreakevenView.tsx` and the folders
`src/views/quote/` and `src/views/breakeven/`, each with its own CSS file. Helpers the
two views share with Q3 and Q4 (margin wording, carriers per year, debounce, the
view-level note, error and skeleton classes, the small segmented toggle) live in
`src/lib/`, `src/hooks/` and `src/styles/views.css` (see Questions 3 and 4 above).

**Q1.** The answer (cheapest total for the chosen speed) sits directly under the
question at `--text-figure`, followed by carrier and service at `--text-lg` and the
margin with a sign and the word "margin" or "loss". Below a heavy rule, the form
(left, 17 rem) and the explanation (right) share a two-column grid that stacks under
52 rem. The form prices live with a 300 ms debounce; the previous answer stays visible
at 55 % opacity while the next one loads, so typing never flashes a skeleton. Each
carrier row is a disclosure button: rank, carrier name in its colour, a stacked bar
(base solid, surcharges hatched, fuel wash with an outline, so the three parts differ
by texture and not only by tint), total and the difference to the cheapest. Line items
carry their source under the label in small muted type. Unavailable services are struck
through and muted, with the reason in words. When dimensional weight sets the billable
weight, a ruled note shows actual, dimensional and billable weight per service. Server
422 messages appear under the input they concern, in `--loss`, and the input gets
`aria-invalid`.

**Q2.** The figure is the lightest weight at which USPS Ground Advantage stops being
cheapest, with a caption naming the distances and rivals; one plain sentence per
distance band (neighbouring bands that read the same are merged) follows. The map is a
hand-built SVG: rows are weights, columns the zone-band midpoints, cell colour is the
winner's carrier colour mixed with its wash in four fixed saving steps (under $1,
$1–3, $3–10, $10+), so the legend means the same on every map. A heavy ink line marks
where USPS stops or starts winning and a dotted line where UPS and FedEx swap; runs
tall enough carry the carrier name. Colour is therefore never the only cue. The grid is
a roving-tabindex `role="grid"` (arrows, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown, Escape closes the
tooltip); hover, tap or focus shows every carrier's total. "Show as table" swaps the
map for a sticky-header table. At 375 px the map fits without horizontal scroll (columns
shrink, headers abbreviate to "z5").
/* Design tokens. See frontend/DESIGN.md for the reasoning. */
:root {
  color-scheme: light;

  /* Paper and ink */
  --paper: #f5f1e8;
  --sheet: #fbf9f4;
  --ink: #1c1b18;
  --ink-muted: #5e5a50;
  --rule: #d9d2c3;
  --rule-strong: #1c1b18;
  --wash: #ebe5d7; /* bar track, hover wash */

  /* Carriers: one fixed colour each, used for text, bars, map cells and lines */
  --carrier-usps: #1f4e9a;
  --carrier-ups: #7a4e0f;
  --carrier-fedex: #9c2a7e;
  --carrier-usps-wash: #dfe7f4;
  --carrier-ups-wash: #efe4d2;
  --carrier-fedex-wash: #f2dfec;

  /* Money */
  --loss: #b3261e;
  --loss-wash: #f7e1de;
  --profit: #1d6b3f;
  --profit-wash: #dcefe2;

  /* Status */
  --mock: #8a5a00;
  --mock-wash: #fbefcf;
  --focus: #1c1b18;
  --focus-halo: #f5f1e8;

  /* Type */
  --font-display: "Newsreader", "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", Georgia, serif;
  --font-ui: "IBM Plex Sans", "Helvetica Neue", Arial, system-ui, sans-serif;

  --text-xs: 0.75rem;
  --text-sm: 0.875rem;
  --text-base: 1rem;
  --text-lg: 1.1875rem;
  --text-xl: clamp(1.375rem, 1.1rem + 1vw, 1.75rem);
  --text-2xl: clamp(1.75rem, 1.2rem + 2vw, 2.625rem);
  --text-figure: clamp(2.75rem, 1.6rem + 4.5vw, 5rem);

  /* Spacing: a 4 px base with a deliberate jump for section breaks */
  --space-1: 0.25rem;
  --space-2: 0.5rem;
  --space-3: 0.75rem;
  --space-4: 1rem;
  --space-5: 1.5rem;
  --space-6: 2rem;
  --space-7: 3rem;
  --space-8: 4.5rem;

  --rail-width: 19rem;
  --measure: 68ch;
  --radius: 2px;

  --duration-fast: 120ms;
  --duration: 220ms;
  --ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);

  --shadow-sheet: 0 -12px 40px rgb(28 27 24 / 0.18);

  /* Q3 cost split: neutral base, a teal ramp for surcharge kinds (strongest = largest kind),
     ink for fuel. Teal sits outside the carrier and money hues. */
  --q3-base: #b7ae9b;
  --q3-sur-1: #0f5f68;
  --q3-sur-2: #2f8c95;
  --q3-sur-3: #6fb5bb;
  --q3-sur-4: #a9d3d5;
  --q3-fuel: #1c1b18;
  /* Q4 drivers: cost up (warm) vs cost down (cool); neither is the loss/profit pair. */
  --q4-up: #a2541f;
  --q4-down: #2f6f86;
}
```

```
import AxeBuilder from "@axe-core/playwright";
import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";
import { loadSample, openApp, settled, showView, type ViewId } from "./helpers";

/**
 * axe on every question view, light and dark. Serious and critical violations fail the test;
 * moderate and minor ones are attached to the report for review. No exclusions: the chart SVGs
 * sit inside aria-hidden wrappers (the caption and "Show as table" carry the content) and pass.
 */
const VIEWS: ViewId[] = ["quote", "breakeven", "blended", "yearly"];
const BLOCKING = new Set(["serious", "critical"]);

for (const scheme of ["light", "dark"] as const) {
  test.describe(`axe, ${scheme}`, () => {
    test.use({ colorScheme: scheme });

    for (const view of VIEWS) {
      test(`${view} has no serious or critical violations`, async ({ page }, info) => {
        await openApp(page);
        await loadSample(page);
        await showView(page, view);
        await settled(page);

        const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
          .withTags(["wcag2a", "wcag2aa", "wcag21a", "wcag21aa", "wcag22aa", "best-practice"])
          .analyze();
        await info.attach("axe-violations.json", {
          body: JSON.stringify(results.violations, null, 2),
          contentType: "application/json",
        });
        const blocking = results.violations
          .filter((v) => BLOCKING.has(v.impact ?? ""))
          .map(
            (v) =>
              `${v.impact} ${v.id}: ${v.help}\n  ${v.nodes
              .slice(0, 5)
              .map((n) => `${n.target.join(" ")}: ${n.failureSummary ?? ""}`)
              .join("\n  ")}`,
          );
        expect(blocking, blocking.join("\n")).toEqual([]);
      });
    }
  });
}
import { test, type Page } from "@playwright/test";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { isMobile, loadSample, openApp, openSettings, setBox, settled, showView, type ViewId } from "./helpers";

/**
 * Full-page captures of every view for the UX review (docs/ux-review.md), run with
 * `npm run e2e:update-screens`. Deterministic: the fixed sample mix, default controls,
 * the default quote form, reduced motion, settled charts and the page scrolled to the top.
 */
const DIR = path.join(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "screenshots");

/** Resolve once nothing inside the charts has changed for a few frames (Recharts animates in). */
async function chartsSettled(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  // A function passed to evaluate, not waitForFunction: the app's CSP forbids string eval.
  await page.evaluate(
    () =>
      new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
        let last = "";
        let same = 0;
        const tick = () => {
          const snap = [...document.querySelectorAll(".recharts-wrapper, .hm__svg")].map((e) => e.innerHTML).join("|");
          same = snap === last ? same + 1 : 0;
          last = snap;
          if (same >= 5) resolve();
          else requestAnimationFrame(tick);
        };
        requestAnimationFrame(tick);
      }),
  );
}

async function capture(page: Page, name: string, project: string, scheme: string): Promise<void> {
  await settled(page);
  await page.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready);
  await chartsSettled(page);
  // The settings rail is sticky: without this it lands mid-page in a full-page capture.
  await page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0, 0));
  await page.evaluate(() => new Promise((r) => requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(r))));
  await page.screenshot({
    path: path.join(DIR, `${name}-${project}-${scheme}.png`),
    fullPage: true,
    animations: "disabled",
    caret: "hide",
  });
}

const VIEWS: { name: string; view: ViewId; setup?: (page: Page) => Promise<void> }[] = [
  {
    name: "q1-typical",
    view: "quote",
    setup: async (page) => {
      // Open the cheapest row so the line items and their sources are in the shot.
      await page.locator(".qrank > li").first().getByRole("button").click();
    },
  },
  { name: "q1-bulky", view: "quote", setup: (page) => setBox(page, "24", "20", "18") },
  { name: "q2", view: "breakeven" },
  { name: "q3", view: "blended" },
  { name: "q4", view: "yearly" },
];

for (const scheme of ["light", "dark"] as const) {
  test.describe(`screens, ${scheme} @screens`, () => {
    test.use({ colorScheme: scheme, contextOptions: { reducedMotion: "reduce" } });

    for (const v of VIEWS) {
      test(v.name, async ({ page }, info) => {
        await openApp(page);
        await loadSample(page);
        await showView(page, v.view);
        await v.setup?.(page);
        await capture(page, v.name, info.project.name, scheme);
      });
    }

    test("settings-sheet", async ({ page }, info) => {
      test.skip(!isMobile(info), "the sheet exists on phones only");
      await openApp(page);
      await loadSample(page);
      await showView(page, "quote");
      await page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0, 0));
      await openSettings(page, info);
      await page.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready);
      await page.screenshot({ path: path.join(DIR, `settings-sheet-${info.project.name}-${scheme}.png`), animations: "disabled", caret: "hide" });
    });
  });
}
import { expect, type Locator, type Page, type Response, type TestInfo } from "@playwright/test";

export type ViewId = "quote" | "breakeven" | "blended" | "yearly";

export const isMobile = (info: TestInfo) => info.project.name === "mobile";

/** Wait for the next answer from an API endpoint, e.g. `nextResponse(page, "/api/quote")`. */
export function nextResponse(page: Page, path: string, method = "POST"): Promise<Response> {
  return page.waitForResponse((r) => new URL(r.url()).pathname === path && r.request().method() === method);
}

/** Open the app (optionally with a query string) and wait until the price lists have loaded. */
export async function openApp(page: Page, search = ""): Promise<void> {
  const meta = nextResponse(page, "/api/meta", "GET");
  await page.goto(`/${search}`);
  expect((await meta).ok()).toBe(true);
  await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1, name: "Parcel Rates" })).toBeVisible();
}

/** Click "Load sample mix" and wait for the strip to show the parcel count. */
export async function loadSample(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  const sample = nextResponse(page, "/api/sample-parcels", "GET");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Load sample mix" }).click();
  expect((await sample).ok()).toBe(true);
  await expect(page.locator(".strip__count")).toContainText("307 parcels");
}

export const tab = (page: Page, view: ViewId): Locator => page.locator(`#tab-${view}`);
export const panel = (page: Page): Locator => page.getByRole("tabpanel");

/** Switch to a question and wait for its API answer. */
export async function showView(page: Page, view: ViewId): Promise<void> {
  if (view === "quote") {
    await tab(page, view).click();
    await expect(page.getByTestId("quote-answer")).toBeVisible();
    return;
  }
  // Q4 asks twice: once with the controls, then again with the next-year increase its first
  // answer suggests. Wait for the second, or the view is still dimmed as "stale".
  const answer =
    view === "yearly"
      ? page.waitForResponse(
          (r) => new URL(r.url()).pathname === "/api/yearly" && "next_year_increase_percent" in (r.request().postDataJSON() ?? {}),
        )
      : nextResponse(page, `/api/${view}`);
  await tab(page, view).click();
  expect((await answer).ok()).toBe(true);
  const id = { breakeven: "breakeven-answer", blended: "q3-answer", yearly: "q4-answer" }[view];
  await expect(page.getByTestId(id)).toBeVisible();
}

/** The settings: the side rail on desktop, the bottom sheet behind "Adjust" on phones. */
export async function openSettings(page: Page, info: TestInfo): Promise<Locator> {
  if (isMobile(info)) {
    await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Adjust" }).click();
    const sheet = page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Assumptions" });
    await expect(sheet).toBeVisible();
    return sheet;
  }
  return page.getByRole("complementary", { name: "Assumptions" });
}

export async function closeSettings(page: Page, info: TestInfo): Promise<void> {
  if (!isMobile(info)) return;
  await page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Assumptions" }).getByRole("button", { name: "Done" }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Assumptions" })).toHaveCount(0);
}

/** The Q1 form, by its accessible name. */
export const quoteForm = (page: Page): Locator => page.getByRole("form", { name: "Your parcel" });

/** Replace a text input's value and wait for the quote the change triggers (debounced 300 ms). */
export async function fillAndQuote(page: Page, input: Locator, value: string): Promise<Response> {
  const quote = nextResponse(page, "/api/quote");
  await input.fill(value);
  return quote;
}

/** Set the Q1 box size and wait for the new quote. */
export async function setBox(page: Page, l: string, w: string, h: string): Promise<void> {
  const form = quoteForm(page);
  await form.getByLabel("Length in inches").fill(l);
  await form.getByLabel("Width in inches").fill(w);
  const quote = nextResponse(page, "/api/quote");
  await form.getByLabel("Height in inches").fill(h);
  expect((await quote).ok()).toBe(true);
  await expect(page.locator(".is-stale")).toHaveCount(0);
}

/** Text of the Q1 answer figure once the answer on screen is fresh. */
export async function quoteTotal(page: Page): Promise<string> {
  await expect(page.locator(".qv__answer")).toHaveAttribute("aria-busy", "false");
  await expect(page.locator(".is-stale")).toHaveCount(0);
  return (await page.getByTestId("quote-answer").innerText()).trim();
}

/** No request in flight, nothing dimmed as stale, and every CSS transition finished. */
export async function settled(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  await expect(page.locator('[aria-busy="true"]')).toHaveCount(0);
  await expect(page.locator(".is-stale")).toHaveCount(0);
  await page.evaluate(() => Promise.all(document.getAnimations().map((a) => a.finished)));
}
```

```
Issues: fuel sliders and "Done" were under 44 px (finding 3, **fixed**).

## Loading and empty states

Not in the screenshot set (captures wait for answers), but covered by tests:
Q3 and Q4 show "Load the sample mix or upload a CSV" with both actions before a
set is loaded (`q3-blended.spec.ts`), Q1 keeps the previous answer dimmed while
the next one loads, and a 422 shows the server's message under the weight
input with `aria-invalid` (`q1-quote.spec.ts`).

## Capture notes

- Captures are deterministic in content (fixed sample, fixed controls,
  reduced motion, CSS transitions finished, charts unchanged for five frames,
  fonts loaded, page scrolled to the top). A recapture can still differ by a
  few thousand anti-aliased pixels, so the images are for review, not pixel
  assertions.
- The README images in `docs/screenshots/` are the desktop light captures
  cropped above the footer and resized to 1200 px wide, plus two phone first
  screens, quantised to 256-colour PNG and passed through `optipng`.

## 2026-10-23 — FedEx 2027 stays as a forward year, flagged (PRs #21, #23)

- FedEx 2027 base rates are published and parsed, but its surcharge-change
  document is not archived, so only the Home Delivery residential charge and
  the January peak rows exist. Rather than drop the year, it stays selectable
  and the UI states that 2027 is FedEx only and that its totals understate
  surcharges (Q1, Q2, Q4 notes; README limitations).

## 2026-10-23 — Typical sample mix (issue #22, PR #25)

- The first sample (300 parcels, 22 % bulky, 13 % expedited, all at the flat
  $9.99) showed 71 % of parcels shipped at a loss even with USPS. That was an
  artefact of the sample, not an insight.
- Owner decision: an illustrative home-goods shop with mostly light ground
  parcels, 7 % bulky, 4 % two-to-three day and 1 % next day, and the expedited
  parcels carrying their own `price_charged` ($19.99 / $39.99), as real shops
  charge more for speed. The default view now opens near break-even (USPS
  margin −$0.31 per parcel, 40 % of parcels at a loss), with the losses in
  bulky boxes, 5–20 lb and far zones. The label "illustrative example" is kept
  in the API and the UI.

## 2026-10-23 — End-to-end tests and screenshots (issue #8, PR #26)

- Playwright pinned to 1.49 so it runs on Node 18; axe scans fail on serious
  or critical violations and now pass at every level.
- Screenshots that passed the UX review are added to the README, at the
  owner's request; remaining UX items are tracked in #27.

## Decisions changed after reviewing agent output

| Decision | What the agent produced | What changed, and why | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Zone bands | My brief told the agents UPS/FedEx zone n = USPS zone n+1 | The USPS agent's DMM reading showed zones 1 and 2 are separate; bands rebuilt from the DMM | Agent log 2026-10-23 08:44; PR #15 |
| Rate-card naming | Amended schema stored UPS Daily Rates and FedEx Standard List Rates as `retail` | Owner: `list` for UPS and FedEx, `retail`/`commercial` for USPS, default commercial | Agent log 2026-10-23 08:10 and 08:18; PR #15 |
| Sample mix | Generator produced a mix with 71 % of parcels at a loss | Owner reversed it to a typical mix with expedited `price_charged` | Issue #22; PR #25 |
| Minimum billable weight | Engine priced oversize parcels at actual or dimensional weight | Review of PR #17 found the 90 lb minimum; added as cited data | Issue #18; PR #24 |

The delivery-area opt-in is not in this table: the transcript shows the agent
proposed it in the schema draft (agent log 2026-10-22 13:23) and the owner
accepted it unchanged, so it is recorded above as a decision, not a reversal.
```

```
.qr--open .qr__chev {

}

.qbar {

}

.qbar__part {

}

.qr__panel {

}

.qitems {

}

.qitems th,
.qitems td {

}

.qitems thead th {

}

}

.qitems .num {

}

}

.qitems tfoot th,
.qitems tfoot td {

}

.qitems__sub {

}

/* ---- dimensional weight ---- */

/* ---- other tiers ---- */
.qtiers ul {

.qtiers li {

@media (max-width: 39.999rem) {

/* Q2, breakeven map (issue #5). */
.bv {

/* ---- legend ---- */
.hml {

.hml__note {

}

/* ---- heatmap ---- */
.hm {

}

.hm__scroll {
  position: relative;

  overflow-y: visible;
}

.hm__svg {
  display: block;

}

  outline: none;
}

  font-size: 12px;

.hm__cell {

}

.hm__cell:focus {
  outline: none;
}

.hm__boundary {
  fill: none;
  stroke: var(--ink);
  stroke-width: 2;
  stroke-linecap: square;
  pointer-events: none;
}

.hm__runlabel {
  font-size: 11px;
  font-weight: 700;

  fill: var(--ink);
  stroke: var(--paper);
  stroke-width: 3px;
  paint-order: stroke;
  pointer-events: none;
}

.hm__focus {
  fill: none;
  stroke: var(--ink);
  stroke-width: 2;
  outline: 2px solid var(--paper);
  pointer-events: none;
}

.hm__tip {
```

```
import { useCallback, useId, useMemo, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { useApi, useLoad } from "./api/ApiContext";
import { isMockMode } from "./api/client";
import { ControlRail, assumptionsLine } from "./components/controls/ControlRail";

import { QuestionTabs } from "./components/QuestionTabs";

import { useParcelSet } from "./hooks/useParcelSet";
import { useUrlState } from "./hooks/useUrlState";
import { useMediaQuery } from "./hooks/useMediaQuery";
import { INERT_WHILE_SHEET, SHEET_QUERY, useSheet } from "./hooks/useSheet";
import { controlsFromMeta, type ViewId } from "./state/urlState";
import type { ViewProps } from "./views/types";
import { QuoteView } from "./views/QuoteView";
import { BreakevenView } from "./views/BreakevenView";
import { BlendedView } from "./views/BlendedView";
import { YearlyView } from "./views/YearlyView";

const VIEW_COMPONENTS: Record<ViewId, (p: ViewProps) => JSX.Element> = {
  quote: QuoteView,
  breakeven: BreakevenView,
  blended: BlendedView,
  yearly: YearlyView,
};


export function App() {
  const api = useApi();
  const [metaAttempt, setMetaAttempt] = useState(0);
  const metaState = useLoad((signal) => api.meta(signal), [api, metaAttempt]);
  const meta = metaState.status === "ok" ? metaState.data : null;
  const metaDefaults = useMemo(() => (meta ? controlsFromMeta(meta.defaults) : null), [meta]);
  const [state, dispatch] = useUrlState(metaDefaults);
  const parcelSet = useParcelSet();
  const isSheet = useMediaQuery(SHEET_QUERY);
  const sheet = useSheet(isSheet);
  const railId = useId();
  const railTitleId = useId();
  const inert = { [INERT_WHILE_SHEET]: "" };
  const mock = isMockMode();

  const fileInputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
  const openFilePicker = useCallback(() => fileInputRef.current?.click(), []);

  const viewProps: ViewProps = {
    controls: state.controls,
    meta,
    parcels: parcelSet.set?.parcels ?? null,
    onLoadSample: parcelSet.loadSample,
    onUploadCsv: openFilePicker,
  };

  return (
    <>
      <a className="skip-link" href="#main" {...inert}>
        Skip to the questions
      </a>
      {mock && (
        <p className="mock-banner" role="note" {...inert}>
          <strong>Mock data.</strong> Recorded example answers from the rate service; they do not change with your inputs.

      )}
      <header className="masthead" {...inert}>
        <div className="masthead__inner">
          <p className="kicker masthead__edition">
            {state.controls.year} published list prices · USPS, UPS, FedEx
          </p>
          <h1 className="masthead__title">Parcel Rates</h1>
          <p className="masthead__deck">
            Which carrier is cheapest for each kind of parcel you ship, and does your flat shipping price still cover
            the real cost after surcharges and yearly increases?
          </p>
        </div>
      </header>

      <div className="mobile-bar" role="region" aria-label="Current assumptions" {...inert}>
        <p className="mobile-bar__line">{assumptionsLine(state)}</p>
        <button
          ref={sheet.toggleRef}
          type="button"
          className="btn mobile-bar__toggle"
          aria-expanded={sheet.open}
          aria-controls={railId}
          onClick={() => sheet.setOpen(!sheet.open)}
        >
          Adjust
        </button>
      </div>

      <div className="layout">
        {sheet.open && (
          <div className="sheet-backdrop" aria-hidden="true" onClick={sheet.close} />

        <aside

          ref={sheet.sheetRef}

          aria-labelledby={railTitleId}
          {...(sheet.open ? { role: "dialog", "aria-modal": true } : {})}
        >
          <div className="rail__head">
            <h2 id={railTitleId} className="kicker rail__title">
              Assumptions

            <button type="button" className="btn btn--quiet rail__close" onClick={sheet.close}>

          </div>
          <ControlRail

            dispatch={dispatch}
            meta={meta}
            metaStatus={metaState.status === "ok" ? "ok" : metaState.status}
            onRetryMeta={() => setMetaAttempt((n) => n + 1)}
          />
        </aside>

        <main id="main" className="main" tabIndex={-1} {...inert}>
          <ParcelSetPanel
            set={parcelSet.set}
```

```
import { useMemo, useRef, useState, type KeyboardEvent } from "react";
import type { BreakevenCell, BreakevenResponse, Carrier, Meta } from "../../api/types";
import { CARRIERS } from "../../api/types";
import { cellGrid, groundName, savingLevel, zoneLabel } from "./readout";
import { useWidth } from "./useWidth";
import { CARRIER_NAME } from "../../lib/carriers";
import { formatInt, formatUsd } from "../../lib/format";

const LEVEL_MIX = [22, 48, 74, 100] as const;

export function cellFill(c: BreakevenCell | null): string {
  if (!c?.winner) return "var(--wash)";
  const v = `var(--carrier-${c.winner.carrier})`;
  const w = `var(--carrier-${c.winner.carrier}-wash)`;
  return `color-mix(in srgb, ${v} ${LEVEL_MIX[savingLevel(c.saving)]}%, ${w})`;
}

function cellLabel(c: BreakevenCell | null, meta: Meta | null, residential: boolean): string {
  if (!c) return "no data";
  const head = `${c.weight_lb} lb, ${formatInt(c.distance_miles)} mi`;
  if (!c.winner) return `${head}: no ground service can carry it`;
  const win = `${groundName(meta, c.winner.carrier, residential)} cheapest at ${formatUsd(c.winner.total)}`;
  const run = c.runner_up
    ? `, ${formatUsd(c.saving)} less than ${groundName(meta, c.runner_up.carrier, residential)}`
    : ", no other carrier to compare";
  return `${head}: ${win}${run}`;
}

import { useEffect, useId, useState } from "react";
import type { Meta } from "../../api/types";
import type { Action, AppState } from "../../state/urlState";
import { fuelDefault, yearOptions } from "../../lib/fuel";
import { FuelSlider } from "./FuelSlider";
import { CARRIER_NAME } from "../../lib/carriers";
import { formatPercent, formatUsd } from "../../lib/format";

export interface ControlRailProps {
  state: AppState;
  dispatch: (a: Action) => void;
  meta: Meta | null;
  metaStatus: "loading" | "ok" | "error" | "idle";
  onRetryMeta: () => void;
}

/** One-line summary of the assumptions, shown in the mobile bar. */
export function assumptionsLine(state: AppState): string {
  const c = state.controls;
  const o = c.fuel_override_percent;
  const fuel = o
    ? `fuel ${[o.ground, o.express].map((v) => (v === undefined ? "default" : formatPercent(v))).join(" / ")}`
    : "fuel default";
  return [String(c.year), `USPS ${c.usps_rate_card}`, fuel, c.peak ? "peak" : null, `${formatUsd(c.flat_price)} charged`]
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join(" · ");
}

function PriceInput({ value, onCommit }: { value: number; onCommit: (n: number) => void }) {
  const id = useId();
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState(value.toFixed(2));
  const [problem, setProblem] = useState<string | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => setDraft(value.toFixed(2)), [value]);

  const commit = () => {
    const cleaned = draft.trim().replace(/^\$/, "");
    const n = Number(cleaned);
    if (cleaned === "" || !Number.isFinite(n) || n < 0 || n > 1000) {
      setProblem("Enter a price between $0 and $1,000");
      return;
    }
    setProblem(null);
    onCommit(Math.round(n * 100) / 100);
  };

  return (
    <div className="control">
      <label htmlFor={id} className="control__label">
        Flat price you charge per parcel
      </label>
      <div className={`money-input ${problem ? "money-input--invalid" : ""}`}>
        <span aria-hidden="true">$</span>
        <input
          id={id}
          inputMode="decimal"
          autoComplete="off"
          value={draft}
          aria-invalid={problem ? true : undefined}
          aria-describedby={`${id}-hint`}
          onChange={(e) => setDraft(e.target.value)}
          onBlur={commit}
          onKeyDown={(e) => {
            if (e.key === "Enter") commit();
          }}
        />
      </div>
      <p id={`${id}-hint`} className={problem ? "control__error" : "control__hint"}>
        {problem ?? "A price_charged column in your CSV overrides this per parcel."}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}

export function ControlRail({ state, dispatch, meta, metaStatus, onRetryMeta }: ControlRailProps) {
  const c = state.controls;
  const years = yearOptions(meta);
  const yearList = years.length > 0 ? years : [{ year: c.year, missing: [] }];
  const yearId = useId();
  const peakId = useId();

  return (
    <div className="rail__body">
      {metaStatus === "loading" && (
        <p className="rail__status" role="status">
          <span className="pulse" aria-hidden="true" /> Loading price lists…
        </p>
      )}
      {metaStatus === "error" && (
        <div className="rail__status rail__status--error" role="alert">
          <p>Price lists did not load. The controls use built-in defaults until the rate service answers.</p>
          <button type="button" className="btn" onClick={onRetryMeta}>
            Try again
          </button>
        </div>
      )}

      <div className="control">
        <label htmlFor={yearId} className="control__label">
          Price list year
        </label>
        <select
          id={yearId}
          className="select"
          value={c.year}
          onChange={(e) => dispatch({ type: "year", year: Number(e.target.value) })}
        >
          {yearList.map(({ year, missing }) => (
            <option key={year} value={year}>
              {year}
              {missing.length > 0 ? ` (no ${missing.map((m) => CARRIER_NAME[m]).join(", ")})` : ""}
            </option>
          ))}
        </select>
      </div>

      <fieldset className="control segmented">
        <legend className="control__label">USPS prices</legend>
        <div className="segmented__options">
          {(
            [
              ["commercial", "Commercial", "online postage"],
              ["retail", "Retail", "Post Office counter"],
            ] as const
          ).map(([value, label, note]) => (
            <label key={value} className="segmented__option">
              <input
                type="radio"
                name="usps-rate-card"
                value={value}
                checked={c.usps_rate_card === value}
                onChange={() => dispatch({ type: "card", card: value })}
              />
              <span className="segmented__text">
                {label}
                <small>{note}</small>
              </span>
            </label>
          ))}
        </div>
      </fieldset>

      <fieldset className="control">
        <legend className="control__label">Fuel surcharge, UPS and FedEx</legend>
        <FuelSlider
          group="ground"
          label="Ground"
          hint="ground services"
          override={c.fuel_override_percent?.ground}
          defaultInfo={fuelDefault(meta, c.year, "ground")}
          onChange={(percent) => dispatch({ type: "fuel", group: "ground", percent })}
          onReset={() => dispatch({ type: "fuelReset", group: "ground" })}
        />
        <FuelSlider
          group="express"
          label="Express"
          hint="2–3 day and next day"
          override={c.fuel_override_percent?.express}
          defaultInfo={fuelDefault(meta, c.year, "express")}
          onChange={(percent) => dispatch({ type: "fuel", group: "express", percent })}
          onReset={() => dispatch({ type: "fuelReset", group: "express" })}
        />
      </fieldset>

      <div className="control switch">
        <input
          id={peakId}
          type="checkbox"
          role="switch"
          checked={c.peak}
          aria-describedby={`${peakId}-hint`}
          onChange={(e) => dispatch({ type: "peak", peak: e.target.checked })}
        />
        <label htmlFor={peakId} className="switch__label">
          Peak season surcharges
        </label>
        <p id={`${peakId}-hint`} className="control__hint switch__hint">
          Prices as of December 10, inside every carrier's peak window.
        </p>
      </div>

      <PriceInput value={c.flat_price} onCommit={(price) => dispatch({ type: "price", price })} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

```
function Answer({ data, answer, kicker }: { data: BlendedResponse; answer: BlendedAnswer; kicker: string }) {
  const { cheapest, others, mixSavingPerParcel, mixSavingTotal } = answer;
  const mix = data.best_mix;
  const mixCounts = Object.entries(mix.parcels_by_carrier)
    .filter(([, n]) => n > 0)
    .sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]);
  return (
    <div className="answer q3-answer">
      <p className="kicker">{kicker}</p>
      <p className="answer__figure" data-testid="q3-answer">
        <span className="carrier-tag" style={{ color: carrierVar(cheapest.carrier) }}>
          {carrierName(cheapest.carrier)}
        </span>{" "}
        {formatUsd(cheapest.cost_per_parcel)}
        <span className="answer__unit"> per parcel</span>
      </p>
      <p className="answer__caption">
        Blended over every parcel at its cheapest {carrierName(cheapest.carrier)} service for the speed it needs.
        {others.length > 0 && " "}
        {others.map((c, i) => (
          <span key={c.carrier}>
            {i > 0 && ", "}
            <strong style={{ color: carrierVar(c.carrier) }}>{carrierName(c.carrier)}</strong> {formatUsd(c.cost_per_parcel)}{" "}
            ({signedUsd(c.cost_per_parcel - cheapest.cost_per_parcel)})
          </span>
        ))}
        {others.length > 0 && "."}
      </p>
      <div className="mix" data-testid="q3-mix">
        <p className="mix__line">
          <span className="mix__label">Best mix</span>{" "}
          <span className="figure mix__figure">{formatUsd(mix.cost_per_parcel)}</span> per parcel, choosing the cheapest
          carrier for each parcel:{" "}
          {mixSavingPerParcel > 0 ? (
            <>
              <strong>{formatUsd(mixSavingPerParcel)} less per parcel</strong> than {carrierName(cheapest.carrier)} alone (
              {formatUsd(mixSavingTotal)} on these parcels).
            </>
          ) : (
            <>no saving over {carrierName(cheapest.carrier)} alone.</>
          )}
        </p>
        <p className="mix__split">
          {mixCounts.map(([c, n], i) => (
            <span key={c}>
              {i > 0 && " · "}
              <span style={{ color: carrierVar(c as Carrier) }}>{carrierName(c)}</span> {formatInt(n)}
            </span>
          ))}
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

function Verdict({ data, answer, controls }: { data: BlendedResponse; answer: BlendedAnswer; controls: ControlsState }) {
  const c = answer.cheapest;
  const loss = c.margin_per_parcel < 0;
  const charged = data.revenue_per_parcel;
  const mixedPrices = Math.abs(charged - controls.flat_price) >= 0.005;
  const rows = [
    ...[...data.carriers].filter((x) => x.parcels_shipped > 0).sort((a, b) => a.cost_per_parcel - b.cost_per_parcel),
  ];
  return (
    <section className={`verdict ${loss ? "verdict--loss" : "verdict--profit"}`} aria-labelledby="q3-verdict">
      <h3 id="q3-verdict" className="verdict__q">
        Does your {formatUsd(controls.flat_price)} shipping price cover the cost?
      </h3>
      <p className="verdict__figure" data-testid="q3-verdict">
        <span className="verdict__word">{loss ? "No." : "Yes."}</span>{" "}
        {loss ? (
          <>
            You lose {formatUsd(-c.margin_per_parcel)} per parcel with {carrierName(c.carrier)}
          </>
        ) : (
          <>
            {formatUsd(c.margin_per_parcel)} margin per parcel with {carrierName(c.carrier)}
          </>
        )}
      </p>
      <p className="verdict__loss-share" data-testid="q3-loss-share">
        {c.parcels_at_loss === 0 ? (
          <>
            Every parcel covers its cost with {carrierName(c.carrier)}
            {data.best_mix.parcels_at_loss > 0 && <>; {formatShare(data.best_mix.loss_share)} would lose money with the best mix</>}.
          </>
        ) : (
          <>
            <strong>{formatShare(c.loss_share)}</strong> of parcels ({formatInt(c.parcels_at_loss)} of {formatInt(c.parcels_shipped)})
            ship at a loss even with the cheapest carrier
            {data.best_mix.loss_share !== c.loss_share && <>; {formatShare(data.best_mix.loss_share)} with the best mix</>}.
          </>
        )}
      </p>
      {mixedPrices && (
        <p className="verdict__note">
          You charge {formatUsd(charged)} per parcel on average: the flat {formatUsd(controls.flat_price)}, and your own
          price on rows that have one.
        </p>
      )}
      <table className="ledger-table margin-table">
        <caption className="visually-hidden">Margin per parcel and share shipped at a loss, per carrier</caption>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th scope="col">Carrier</th>
            <th scope="col" className="num">
    .map((c) => ({ c, ch: periodChange(c, ref) }))
    .filter((x) => x.ch !== null);

  return (
    <div className={stale ? "is-stale" : undefined}>
      <div className="answer q4-answer">
        <p className="kicker">
          {carrierName(pick.carrier)}, your cheapest carrier in {ref} · {formatInt(pick.parcels_used)} parcels
          {change && (
            <>
              {" "}
              · <span className="q4-since">change since {change.fromYear}</span>
            </>
          )}
        </p>
        {change ? (
          <>
            <p className="answer__figure" data-testid="q4-answer">
              <span className="carrier-tag" style={{ color: carrierVar(pick.carrier) }}>
                {carrierName(pick.carrier)}
              </span>{" "}
              {signedPct(change.percent)}
            </p>
            <p className="answer__caption" data-testid="q4-caption">
              {formatUsd(change.from)} → {formatUsd(change.to)} per parcel from {change.fromYear} to {change.toYear} (
              {signedUsd(change.dollars)}).{" "}
              {change.announcedPercent !== null ? (
                <>
                  The increases {carrierName(pick.carrier)} announced compound to{" "}
                  <strong>{signedPct(change.announcedPercent)}</strong> over the same years, so your mix rose{" "}
                  <strong>
                    {Math.abs(change.percent - change.announcedPercent).toFixed(1)} points{" "}
                    {change.percent >= change.announcedPercent ? "more" : "less"}
                  </strong>{" "}
                  than announced.
                </>
              ) : (
                <>No announced increase is recorded for every year, so there is nothing to compare against.</>
              )}
            </p>
            {others.length > 0 && (
              <p className="q4-others">
                Same years for the others:{" "}
                {others.map(({ c, ch }, i) => (
                  <span key={c.carrier}>
                    {i > 0 && " · "}
                    <strong style={{ color: carrierVar(c.carrier) }}>{carrierName(c.carrier)}</strong> {signedPct(ch!.percent)}
                    {ch!.announcedPercent !== null && <> (announced {signedPct(ch!.announcedPercent)})</>}
                  </span>
                ))}
              </p>
            )}
          </>
        ) : (
          <>
            <p className="answer__figure" data-testid="q4-single-year">
              <span className="carrier-tag" style={{ color: carrierVar(pick.carrier) }}>
                {carrierName(pick.carrier)}

        )}
      </div>

      <NextYear data={data} pick={pick.carrier} increase={increase} onIncrease={onIncrease} />
```

```
import sys
def lin(c):
    c/=255
    return c/12.92 if c<=0.04045 else ((c+0.055)/1.055)**2.4
def L(h):
    h=h.lstrip('#'); r,g,b=(int(h[i:i+2],16) for i in (0,2,4))
    return 0.2126*lin(r)+0.7152*lin(g)+0.0722*lin(b)
def cr(a,b):
    la,lb=sorted([L(a),L(b)],reverse=True); return (la+0.05)/(lb+0.05)
def mix(a,b,p):  # p% of a in b, srgb
    a=a.lstrip('#');b=b.lstrip('#')
    return '#'+''.join('%02x'%round(int(a[i:i+2],16)*p/100+int(b[i:i+2],16)*(100-p)/100) for i in (0,2,4))
if __name__=='__main__':
    for line in sys.stdin:
        line=line.strip()
        if not line: continue
        name,fg,*bgs=line.split()
        print(f"{name:18} {fg}  " + "  ".join(f"{bg}:{cr(fg,bg):5.2f}" for bg in bgs))
EOF
```

- `command`:

```
cd ~/parcel-rates-label-redesign/frontend && cat > /tmp/claude-1000/-home-aivuk-parcel-rates/05ded788-f16a-40ee-858c-7207e1e0ae3d/scratchpad/head.md <<'EOF'
# Visual direction: the shipping label

The dashboard reads like the one printed object every parcel sender already
knows: the shipping label. Stark white stock, heavy black rules that cut the
page into zones, condensed bold figures, receipt-style monospaced line items,
and a single accent, safety orange, that appears only when the answer is a loss.

It replaces the earlier "shipping ledger" direction (warm cream paper, a soft
newspaper serif), which read like a generic AI-product page; see
`docs/DECISIONS.md`, 2026-10-23, "Shipping-label redesign".

## Why it fits

The user is a shop owner deciding where a few dollars per parcel go. A label
is built to be read in a second at arm's length: the service class sits in a
black box, the zones are separated by thick rules, and everything else is
small, uppercase and orderly. That is exactly the hierarchy the dashboard
needs: the answer in the largest, heaviest type; the assumptions in a strip of
small labelled values like a label's header; the evidence (line items, rates,
citations) in a monospaced receipt underneath. Nothing on the page is
decoration except the barcode stripe in the header, which is the one cue that
says "label" before a word is read.

## Hierarchy

1. **The answer** (cheapest carrier, cost per parcel, margin): Barlow Condensed
   700, `--text-figure`, tabular figures. On Q3 and Q4 the figure is a
   **stamp**: paper-coloured figure on an ink block, like the service-class box
   on a label (`.answer__figure--stamp`).
2. **The question** each section answers: Barlow Condensed 600, `--text-xl`.
3. **The owner's parcel set**: once loaded, a one-line strip (count, share to
   homes, speed split) with the full summary behind "Details", so the
   questions and the answer stay above the fold, also on a phone.

### Rule for every question view (issues #5 and #6)

The answer is the largest element of its section. Put it first under the
question, in `.answer > .answer__figure` (`--text-figure`), with a short
`.answer__caption` saying what it is ("UPS Ground, $8.41 per parcel, $1.58
margin"). Nothing else in the section, including the question (`--text-xl`),
chart titles and table figures, may be set larger. Charts and tables come
after the answer and explain it.
4. **Assumptions** (year, rate card, fuel, peak, flat price): on desktop a
   **label header strip** across the top of the page, under the masthead:
   uppercase `--text-xs` labels, bold values, no card or border box, one heavy
   rule beneath. Below 64 rem it is the bottom sheet behind a one-line summary
   bar, as before.

## Zones and rules

The page is divided like a label: **2 px ink rules (`--rule-heavy`) between
major zones** (masthead, assumptions strip, parcel set, question tabs, each
block inside a question) and **1 px hairlines (`--rule`) inside tables and
lists**. No cards, no shadows on the page itself, square corners
(`--radius: 0`). The only shadow is the mobile sheet, which really does sit
above the page.

## Palette (`src/styles/tokens.css`)

Cool neutrals only: no cream or warm cast on any surface in either theme.

| Token | Light | Dark | Use | Contrast on `--paper` (light / dark) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--paper` | `#FFFFFF` | `#0F1113` | page | — |
| `--sheet` | `#F3F4F2` | `#191C1F` | strip inputs, sheet, raised panels | — |
| `--ink` | `#111111` | `#ECEEEA` | text, heavy rules, stamp block, focus ring | 18.9 / 16.2 |
| `--ink-muted` | `#5B6066` | `#A6ACB2` | secondary text, labels | 6.3 / 8.3 (5.8 / 7.5 on `--sheet`) |
| `--rule` | `#D3D6D9` | `#34393E` | hairlines inside tables and lists | — |
| `--carrier-usps` | `#1F4E9A` | `#7FA8EE` | USPS everywhere | 8.0 / 7.9 |
| `--carrier-ups` | `#7A4E0F` | `#D9A35A` | UPS everywhere | 7.2 / 8.4 |
| `--carrier-fedex` | `#9C2A7E` | `#E68AC9` | FedEx everywhere | 6.9 / 8.0 |
| `--accent` | `#E8590C` | `#E8590C` | the loss verdict only (rule, figure ≥ 24 px) | 3.6 / 5.3 |
| `--loss` | `#C2410C` | `#E8590C` | small loss text (tables, "loss", errors) | 5.2 / 5.3 |
| `--profit` | `#1D6B3F` | `#6FCB94` | positive margin | 6.5 / 9.6 |
| `--mock` | `#8A5A00` | `#E8B860` | the mock-data banner only | 5.9 / 10.3 |

Ratios were measured with the WCAG 2 relative-luminance formula and are
against `--paper`; every text colour also clears 4.5:1 on `--sheet`
(lowest: `--loss` 4.7 light, `--accent` 4.8 dark). `--accent` on white is
3.6:1, so in light mode it is used only for the verdict figure (≥ 24 px bold,
AA large text needs 3:1) and the verdict rule (non-text, 3:1); smaller loss
text uses `--loss`, the same orange darkened to pass 4.5:1. The pink wash
behind the verdict is gone: the verdict is a white zone with a heavy accent
rule.

Carrier hues follow the brands loosely (postal blue, brown, purple) so the
owner recognises them without a legend. Blue and purple are close for some
colour-vision deficiencies, so colour is never the only cue: every carrier
mark carries its name or initial, and money always carries a sign and the word
"loss" or "margin". Inside a stamp, the carrier name sits in a small carrier-
coloured box with paper-coloured text (white on the carrier colour: 8.0 / 7.2
/ 6.9 in light; dark text on the light carrier tints in dark mode), because
the carrier colours themselves are too dark to read on the ink block.

Each carrier also has a `-wash` tint for backgrounds and heatmap cells
(issue #5 mixes between the wash and the full colour). The washes are clean,
hue-true tints chosen for white paper, not the old beige-cast ones.

## Type

- **Barlow Condensed** 600 and 700 (`--font-display`) for questions, figures
  and the stamp. A condensed grotesque is what labels use for service class
  and tracking text; it sets big numbers narrow, so the answer can be large on
  a phone.
- **IBM Plex Sans** 400, 500 and 600 (`--font-ui`) for the interface: labels,
  controls, captions.
- **IBM Plex Mono** 400 and 500 (`--font-mono`) for line items, tables and
  citations, receipt style.

One Google Fonts request for the three families, only the weights above, with
`display=swap`; fallbacks are Arial Narrow, Helvetica/Arial and the system
monospace. Every figure uses `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` so columns
of prices line up (set on `body`, repeated on figure classes).

## Spacing and shape

A 4 px base (`--space-1` … `--space-8`: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 72 px) with a
deliberate jump to 48-72 px between sections, so sections read as zones.
Corners are square. Separation comes from rules, not from boxes or shadows.

## Texture

One CSS-generated barcode stripe (`repeating-linear-gradient` of uneven ink
bars) in the masthead, `aria-hidden`, at reduced opacity. It is the only
decorative element on the page; nothing else carries texture.

## Motion

Only opacity and transform, 120-220 ms, for the sheet and tab underline. All
of it is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
```

```
cd ~/parcel-rates-label-redesign && python3 - <<'EOF'
from PIL import Image
src='frontend/e2e/screenshots/'; dst='docs/screenshots/'
def footer_top(im):
    g=im.convert('L'); w,h=g.size; px=g.load()
    for y in range(h-1, h//3, -1):
        dark=sum(1 for x in range(0,w,4) if px[x,y]<60)
        if dark > 0.6*(w/4): return y
    return h
def save(im,name):
    im.convert('RGB').quantize(256, method=Image.Quantize.MEDIANCUT, dither=Image.Dither.NONE).save(dst+name, optimize=True)
for s,d in [('q1-typical','q1-quote'),('q2','q2-breakeven'),('q3','q3-blended'),('q4','q4-yearly')]:
    im=Image.open(src+f'{s}-desktop-light.png'); y=footer_top(im)
    im=im.crop((0,0,im.width,y-16)); im=im.resize((1200, round(im.height*1200/im.width)), Image.LANCZOS)
    save(im,f'{d}-desktop.png'); print(d, im.size, 'footer at', y)
for s,d in [('q1-typical-mobile-light','q1-quote-mobile'),('q3-mobile-dark','q3-blended-mobile-dark')]:
    im=Image.open(src+s+'.png'); save(im.crop((0,0,750,1624)), d+'.png'); print(d)
EOF
optipng -quiet -o2 docs/screenshots/*.png && ls -la docs/screenshots
```

```
## Summary

Replaces the warm-cream / Newsreader "shipping ledger" look, which read like a generic AI-product page, with a **shipping-label** direction. It keeps the hierarchy, the answer-first rule, the carrier colours and the accessibility bar.

- **DESIGN.md first.** It sets out the new direction, with a palette table of measured WCAG contrast in both themes.
- **Tokens and fonts.**
  - Paper is `#FFFFFF` / `#0F1113`, with cool greys only.
  - Safety orange `#E8590C` is used for the loss verdict only. Small loss text uses `--loss` `#C2410C`, the same orange darkened, because the accent passes on white only as large text (3.6:1).
  - The pink box behind the verdict is gone.
  - Barlow Condensed 600/700 replaces Newsreader for display and figures. IBM Plex Mono is used for tables, line items and citations. There is one font request.
- **Rules.** 2 px ink rules separate the major zones; tables and lists use hairlines.
- **Assumptions strip.** On desktop the assumptions sit in a label header strip: uppercase labels, bold values, no card, one heavy rule beneath. Phones keep the bottom sheet.
- **Stamp.** The Q3 and Q4 answers are stamps: a paper figure on an ink block. The carrier name sits in a box of the carrier's colour.
- **Barcode stripe.** A CSS barcode stripe in the masthead is the only decoration.
- **Heatmap.** The lightest saving step holds 45 % of the carrier colour (was 22 %), mixed in oklch with cleaner washes, so cells no longer go pastel or beige on white.
```

```
import { useRef, type KeyboardEvent, type ReactNode } from "react";
import type { ViewId } from "../state/urlState";
import { QUESTIONS } from "../views/types";

export interface QuestionTabsProps {
  active: ViewId;
  onSelect: (id: ViewId) => void;
  renderPanel: (id: ViewId) => ReactNode;
}

const tabId = (id: ViewId) => `tab-${id}`;
const panelId = (id: ViewId) => `panel-${id}`;

/** WAI-ARIA tabs with automatic activation; arrow keys, Home and End move between questions. */
export function QuestionTabs({ active, onSelect, renderPanel }: QuestionTabsProps) {
  const refs = useRef<Partial<Record<ViewId, HTMLButtonElement | null>>>({});
  const activeDef = QUESTIONS.find((q) => q.id === active) ?? QUESTIONS[0]!;

  const onKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    const i = QUESTIONS.findIndex((q) => q.id === active);
    const last = QUESTIONS.length - 1;
    const next =
      e.key === "ArrowRight" ? (i === last ? 0 : i + 1)
      : e.key === "ArrowLeft" ? (i === 0 ? last : i - 1)
      : e.key === "Home" ? 0
      : e.key === "End" ? last
      : null;
    if (next === null) return;
    e.preventDefault();
    const id = QUESTIONS[next]!.id;
    onSelect(id);
    refs.current[id]?.focus();
  };

  return (
    <div className="questions">
      <div className="questions__tabs" role="tablist" aria-label="Questions" onKeyDown={onKeyDown}>
        {QUESTIONS.map((q) => (
          <button
            key={q.id}
            ref={(el) => {
              refs.current[q.id] = el;
            }}
            id={tabId(q.id)}
            type="button"
            role="tab"
            aria-selected={q.id === active}
            aria-controls={panelId(q.id)}
            tabIndex={q.id === active ? 0 : -1}
            className="questions__tab"
            onClick={() => onSelect(q.id)}
          >
            <span className="questions__num">{String(q.number).padStart(2, "0")}</span>
            <span className="questions__short">{q.short}</span>
          </button>
        ))}
      </div>
      <section
        id={panelId(activeDef.id)}
        role="tabpanel"
        aria-labelledby={tabId(activeDef.id)}
        className="questions__panel"
        tabIndex={0}
      >
        <p className="kicker">Question {activeDef.number}</p>
        <h2 className="questions__question">{activeDef.question}</h2>
        {renderPanel(activeDef.id)}
      </section>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```
import { useEffect, useId, useMemo, useRef, useState, type RefObject } from "react";
import type { ZoneBand } from "../../api/types";
import { TIERS } from "../../api/types";
import { CSV_TEMPLATE } from "../../lib/parcelCsv";
import { summarize, type ParcelSummary as Summary } from "../../lib/summary";
import type { ParcelSet, ParcelSetStatus } from "../../hooks/useParcelSet";
import { ParcelSummary } from "./ParcelSummary";
import { formatInt, formatShare, TIER_NAME } from "../../lib/format";

export interface ParcelSetPanelProps {
  set: ParcelSet | null;
  status: ParcelSetStatus;
  /** Zone bands from /api/meta; the USPS ones bucket the distance distribution. */
  zoneBands?: ZoneBand[];
  onLoadSample: () => void;
  onLoadFile: (file: File) => void;
  onClear: () => void;
  /** The CSV file input, so the question views' "Upload CSV" buttons can open the same picker. */
  fileInputRef?: RefObject<HTMLInputElement>;
}

const TEMPLATE_HREF = `data:text/csv;charset=utf-8,${encodeURIComponent(CSV_TEMPLATE)}`;
const MAX_LISTED = 12;

function Problems({ status }: { status: Extract<ParcelSetStatus, { kind: "error" | "notice" }> }) {
  const shown = status.problems.slice(0, MAX_LISTED);
  const rest = status.problems.length - shown.length;
  return (
    <div
      className={`problems ${status.kind === "error" ? "problems--error" : "problems--notice"}`}
      role={status.kind === "error" ? "alert" : "status"}
    >
      <p className="problems__title">{status.message}</p>
      {shown.length > 0 && (
        <ul className="problems__list">
          {shown.map((p, i) => (
            <li key={i}>
              <span className="problems__where">{p.row === null ? "File" : `Row ${p.row}`}</span>
              <span>{p.message}</span>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}
      {rest > 0 && <p className="problems__more">and {rest} more. Fix these first; the rest often share the same cause.</p>}
    </div>
  );
}

/** One line: count, share to homes, speed split. */
function StripFacts({ summary }: { summary: Summary }) {
  return (
    <p className="strip__facts">
      <span className="strip__count">
        <span className="figure">{formatInt(summary.parcels)}</span> parcels
      </span>
      <span>{formatShare(summary.residentialShare)} to homes</span>
      <span>
        {TIERS.filter((t) => summary.byTier[t] > 0)
          .map((t) => `${formatShare(summary.byTier[t])} ${TIER_NAME[t].toLowerCase()}`)
          .join(" · ")}
      </span>
    </p>
  );
}

export function ParcelSetPanel({ set, status, zoneBands, onLoadSample, onLoadFile, onClear, fileInputRef }: ParcelSetPanelProps) {
  const fileId = useId();
  const headingId = useId();
  const detailsId = useId();
  const ownRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
  const inputRef = fileInputRef ?? ownRef;
  const summary = useMemo(() => (set ? summarize(set.parcels, zoneBands) : null), [set, zoneBands]);
  const busy = status.kind === "loading";
  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false);

  // A newly loaded set starts collapsed, so the questions stay above the fold.
  useEffect(() => setExpanded(false), [set]);

  const fileInput = (
    <input
      ref={inputRef}
      id={fileId}
      className="visually-hidden"
      type="file"
      accept=".csv,text/csv"
      disabled={busy}
      onChange={(e) => {
        const file = e.target.files?.[0];
        if (file) onLoadFile(file);
        if (inputRef.current) inputRef.current.value = "";
      }}
    />
  );
  const uploadLabel = (text: string) => (
    <label htmlFor={fileId} className="btn file-btn">
      {busy && status.what === "file" ? "Reading file…" : text}
    </label>
  );
  const sampleButton = (
    <button type="button" className={`btn ${set ? "" : "btn--primary"}`} onClick={onLoadSample} disabled={busy}>
      {busy && status.what === "sample" ? "Loading sample…" : set ? "Use the sample mix" : "Load sample mix"}
    </button>
  );
  const templateLink = (
    <a className="btn btn--quiet" href={TEMPLATE_HREF} download="parcel-set-template.csv">
      CSV template
    </a>
  );
  const problems = (status.kind === "error" || status.kind === "notice") && <Problems status={status} />;

  if (!set || !summary) {
    return (
      <section className="parcels" aria-labelledby={headingId} aria-busy={busy}>
        <header className="parcels__head">
          <h2 id={headingId} className="parcels__title">
            Your parcels
          </h2>
          <div className="parcels__actions">
            {sampleButton}
            {fileInput}
            {uploadLabel("Upload CSV")}
            {templateLink}
          </div>
        </header>
        {problems}
        <div className="parcels__empty">
          <p className="parcels__empty-lead">No parcels loaded yet.</p>
          <p>
            Questions 3 and 4 price your whole mix. Load the sample (an illustrative home-goods shop, not real data) to explore, or upload a CSV with one row per kind
            of parcel: weight, distance, home or business, speed, and how many you ship.
          </p>
        </div>
      </section>
    );
  }

  return (
    <section className="parcels parcels--loaded" aria-labelledby={headingId} aria-busy={busy}>
      <div className="strip">
        <div className="strip__main">
          <h2 id={headingId} className="kicker strip__title">
            Your parcels
            <span className="strip__source"> · {set.source === "sample" ? "sample mix, an example" : set.name}</span>
          </h2>
          <StripFacts summary={summary} />
        </div>
        <div className="strip__actions">
          <button
            type="button"
            className="btn"
            aria-expanded={expanded}
            aria-controls={detailsId}
            onClick={() => setExpanded((e) => !e)}
          >
            {expanded ? "Hide details" : "Details"}
          </button>
          {fileInput}
          {uploadLabel("Replace CSV")}
        </div>
      </div>
      {problems}
      <div id={detailsId} className="parcels__details" hidden={!expanded}>
        {set.description && <p className="parcels__source">{set.description}</p>}
        <ParcelSummary summary={summary} />
        <div className="parcels__actions">
          {sampleButton}
          {templateLink}
          <button type="button" className="btn btn--quiet" onClick={onClear}>
            Clear the set
          </button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}
import { useId } from "react";
import type { FuelGroup } from "../../api/types";
import { FUEL_MAX, FUEL_MIN } from "../../state/urlState";
import type { FuelDefaultInfo } from "../../lib/fuel";
import { formatPercent } from "../../lib/format";

export interface FuelSliderProps {
  group: FuelGroup;
  label: string;
  hint: string;
  override: number | undefined;
  defaultInfo: FuelDefaultInfo | null;
  onChange: (percent: number) => void;
  onReset: () => void;
}

const STEP = 0.25;

export function FuelSlider({ group, label, hint, override, defaultInfo, onChange, onReset }: FuelSliderProps) {
  const id = useId();
  const value = override ?? defaultInfo?.percent ?? 0;
  const isOverridden = override !== undefined;
  const markerLeft = defaultInfo ? ((defaultInfo.percent - FUEL_MIN) / (FUEL_MAX - FUEL_MIN)) * 100 : null;

  return (
    <div className={`fuel ${isOverridden ? "fuel--overridden" : ""}`} data-group={group}>
      <div className="fuel__head">
        <label htmlFor={id} className="fuel__label">
          {label}
        </label>
        <output htmlFor={id} className="fuel__value">
          {formatPercent(value)}
        </output>
      </div>
      <div className="fuel__track">
        <input
          id={id}
          type="range"
          min={FUEL_MIN}
          max={FUEL_MAX}
          step={STEP}
          value={value}
          aria-describedby={`${id}-hint`}
          aria-valuetext={`${formatPercent(value)}${isOverridden ? "" : ", the year's default"}`}
          onChange={(e) => onChange(Number(e.target.value))}
        />
        {markerLeft !== null && (
          <span className="fuel__marker" style={{ left: `${markerLeft}%` }} aria-hidden="true" />
        )}
      </div>
      <div className="fuel__foot" id={`${id}-hint`}>
        {defaultInfo ? (
          <span>
            Year default {formatPercent(defaultInfo.percent)}, {hint}
            {defaultInfo.proxyCarriers.length > 0 && "; UPS uses the FedEx history"}
          </span>
        ) : (
          <span>No published default for this year</span>
        )}
        {isOverridden && (
          <button type="button" className="btn btn--quiet fuel__reset" onClick={onReset}>
            Reset<span className="visually-hidden"> {label.toLowerCase()} fuel to the default</span>
          </button>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```
import type { Meta, Parcel } from "../api/types";
import type { ControlsState, ViewId } from "../state/urlState";
import type { ParcelActions } from "../components/NeedParcels";

/** What every question view receives. Every question view implements this contract. */
export interface ViewProps extends ParcelActions {
  controls: ControlsState;
  meta: Meta | null;
  /** The loaded parcel set, or null when none is loaded (Q3, Q4 need one). */
  parcels: Parcel[] | null;
}

export interface QuestionDef {
  id: ViewId;
  number: number;
  short: string;
  question: string;
  /** Kicker over the answer figure, e.g. "Cheapest for this parcel". */
  answerLabel: string;
  /** Shape of the answer figure while it is not computed. */
  answerBlank: string;
  answerSlot: string;
  needsParcels: boolean;
  issue: number;
}

export const QUESTIONS: readonly QuestionDef[] = [
  {
    id: "quote",
    number: 1,
    short: "Quote a parcel",
    question:
      "For one parcel, which service is cheapest once surcharges are included, and what are the line items of that price?",
    answerLabel: "Cheapest for this parcel",
    answerBlank: "$—.——",
    answerSlot: "Cheapest service per carrier for the chosen speed, ranked, with base, each surcharge, fuel, and the margin against your flat price.",
    needsParcels: false,
    issue: 5,
  },
  {
    id: "breakeven",
    number: 2,
    short: "Breakeven map",
    question: "Where does USPS stop being cheaper than UPS or FedEx ground, by weight and distance?",
    answerLabel: "Where USPS stops winning",
    answerBlank: "— lb",
    answerSlot: "A weight × distance map coloured by the winning ground carrier, with the breakeven lines in plain words.",
    needsParcels: false,
    issue: 5,
  },
  {
    id: "blended",
    number: 3,
    short: "Blended cost",
    question:
      "Across all your parcels, what does each carrier cost per parcel, and how much of that is surcharges rather than base rate?",
    answerLabel: "Best blended cost per parcel",
    answerBlank: "$—.——",
    answerSlot: "Blended cost per parcel per carrier, base vs surcharges vs fuel, margin against your price and the share shipped at a loss.",
    needsParcels: true,
    issue: 6,
  },
  {
    id: "yearly",
    number: 4,
    short: "Year over year",
    question:
      "How did that cost change each year under the published prices, against the increase carriers announced, and which parcels drove it?",
    answerLabel: "Change in cost per parcel",
    answerBlank: "+—%",
    answerSlot: "Cost per parcel per carrier per year against the announced increase, the segments that drove each change, and a projection for next year.",
    needsParcels: true,
    issue: 6,
  },
] as const;
```

```
## Hierarchy

1. **The answer** (cheapest carrier, cost per parcel, margin): Barlow Condensed
   700, `--text-figure`, tabular figures. On Q3 and Q4 the figure is a
   **stamp**: paper-coloured figure on an ink block, like the service-class box
   on a label (`.answer__figure--stamp`).
2. **The question** each section answers: Barlow Condensed 600, `--text-xl`.
3. **The owner's parcel set**: once loaded, a one-line strip (count, share to
   homes, speed split) with the full summary behind "Details", so the
   questions and the answer stay above the fold, also on a phone.

### Rule for every question view (issues #5 and #6)

The answer is the largest element of its section. Put it first under the
question, in `.answer > .answer__figure` (`--text-figure`), with a short
`.answer__caption` saying what it is ("UPS Ground, $8.41 per parcel, $1.58
margin"). Nothing else in the section, including the question (`--text-xl`),
chart titles and table figures, may be set larger. Charts and tables come
after the answer and explain it.
4. **Assumptions** (year, rate card, fuel, peak, flat price): on desktop a
   **label header strip** across the top of the page, under the masthead:
   uppercase `--text-xs` labels, bold values, no card or border box, one heavy
   rule beneath. Below 64 rem it is the bottom sheet behind a one-line summary
   bar, as before.

## Zones and rules

The page is divided like a label: **2 px ink rules (`--rule-heavy`) between
major zones** (masthead, assumptions strip, parcel set, question tabs, each
block inside a question) and **1 px hairlines (`--rule`) inside tables and
lists**. No cards, no shadows on the page itself, square corners
(`--radius: 0`). The only shadow is the mobile sheet, which really does sit
above the page.
## Texture

One CSS-generated barcode stripe (`repeating-linear-gradient` of uneven ink
bars) in the masthead, `aria-hidden`, at reduced opacity. It is the only
decorative element on the page; nothing else carries texture.

## Motion
```

All five changes are in, one commit each, on branch `compact-top`. Nothing is pushed yet. At 1440 px the Q1 answer now starts about 360 px from the top instead of about 690, and the Q3 loss verdict is on the first screen.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Masthead | 222 px | 90 px |
| Tab row, 1440 px | starts at 423 px | starts at 106 px |
| Q1 answer, 1440 px | 687 px | ~360 px |
| Q3 answer, 1440 px | ~690 px | 271 px |

1. **Masthead:** one band with the title and eyebrow on one line and the subtitle as a single muted line under them. The barcode is now a small mark at the start of the eyebrow; phones hide it along with the eyebrow.
2. **Rail:** from 1280 px the assumptions sit in a 260 px left rail that stays in view as you scroll. The fields are stacked and styled like the strip, and the questions start at the top beside it. From 1024 to 1279 px it's still the strip; below 1024 px, the bottom sheet.
3. **Help texts:** they all moved into one "About these assumptions" disclosure at the bottom of the rail, strip or sheet. The fuel sliders keep a short "Default 26.25%" under them, since that's a value. Screen readers still hear each explanation with its control, and price errors still show inline.
4. **Parcels in the tab row:** "307 parcels · sample mix" sits left of the tabs, with Details and Replace CSV on the right. The share going to homes and the speed split moved into Details. Below 1024 px the parcel line and its buttons take a row above the tabs. The tabs are kept separate from the parcel heading so screen readers don't announce them as part of "Your parcels".
5. **Short questions:** headings are now "Cheapest service for one parcel", "Where USPS stops being cheapest", "What your parcels cost per carrier" and "How your cost changed year to year". The full sentence is a muted caption under the answer. I dropped the "Question N" label, since the tab already shows the number.

```
# Quotes every parcel for every carrier and year without caching: about 1 s per
# 1,000 parcels on a laptop. Requests are capped at 10,000 parcels (api/models.py);
# a small shop's monthly mix of a few thousand parcels answers in a few seconds.
def yearly(
    tables: RateTables,
    parcels: list[Parcel],
    controls: Controls,
    next_year_increase_percent: float | None = None,
) -> dict:
    result = []
    for carrier in tables.carriers():
        years = tables.years_for(carrier)
        per_year: dict[int, list[Quote | None]] = {}
        for y in years:
            cy = replace(controls, year=y, as_of=None)
            per_year[y] = per_parcel_quotes(tables, carrier, parcels, cy, year=y)

        # Like-for-like: only parcels the carrier can ship in every year.
        keep = [i for i in range(len(parcels)) if all(per_year[y][i] is not None for y in years)]
        used = [parcels[i] for i in keep]
        n = sum(p.quantity for p in used)
        excluded = sum(p.quantity for p in parcels) - n

        rows = []
        prev_y: int | None = None
        prev_cost: Decimal | None = None
        prev_conditions: set[str] = set()
        for y in years:
            conditions = conditions_in_force(tables, carrier, y, replace(controls, year=y, as_of=None))
            missing = sorted(prev_conditions - conditions)
            quotes = [per_year[y][i] for i in keep]
            totals = Totals()
            for p, q in zip(used, quotes):
                totals.add(q, p.quantity)
            cost = totals.total / n if n else ZERO
            services = sorted({q.service_id for q in quotes})
            row = {
                "year": y,
                "as_of": quotes[0].as_of.isoformat() if quotes else None,
                "cost_per_parcel": _r(cost),
                "summary": summarize(totals),
                "services_used": services,
                "change_vs_previous": None,
                "announced_increase": announced_increase(
                    tables, carrier, y, services, controls.usps_rate_card
                ),
                "drivers": None,
                "fuel": fuel_used(tables, carrier, y, controls),
                "warnings": (
                    [f"No {y} rules recorded for: {', '.join(missing)}; surcharges may be understated"]
                    if missing
                    else []
                ),
            }
            if prev_y is not None and n:
                diff = cost - prev_cost
                row["change_vs_previous"] = {
                    "from_year": prev_y,
                    "dollars_per_parcel": _r(diff),
                    "percent": _r(diff / prev_cost * 100, "0.01") if prev_cost else None,
                }
                prev_quotes = [per_year[prev_y][i] for i in keep]
                row["drivers"] = _drivers(tables, used, prev_quotes, quotes, n)
            rows.append(row)
            prev_y, prev_cost, prev_conditions = y, cost, conditions

        projected = None
        if next_year_increase_percent is not None and rows and n:
            last = rows[-1]
            factor = Decimal(1) + Decimal(str(next_year_increase_percent)) / Decimal(100)
            projected = {
                "year": last["year"] + 1,
                "increase_percent": next_year_increase_percent,
                "cost_per_parcel": _r(prev_cost * factor),
            }
        result.append(
            {
                "carrier": carrier,
                "parcels_used": n,
                "parcels_excluded": excluded,
                "years": rows,
                "projected": projected,
            }
        )
    return {"carriers": result}
```
