- `content`:

```
"""Collect the USPS domestic zone chart for every origin 3-digit ZIP prefix (issue #9).

USPS publishes zones per origin ZIP3 through the Domestic Zone Chart tool on postcalc.usps.com,
which answers with JSON: destination ZIP3 ranges and their zone. This script

1. fetches the chart of a seed origin (100, New York) and expands its destination ranges into
   the list of ZIP3 prefixes, which is the list of origins to collect (discovery by rule);
2. fetches each origin's chart once, sequentially and politely (pause with jitter, retries
   with backoff, identifying User-Agent), resumable: a chart already on disk is not fetched
   again. Raw charts go to data/raw/usps/zones/charts/<zip3>.json (not in git, like the PDFs),
   each listed with its URL, checksum and effective date in data/raw/usps/zones/charts.csv;
3. writes data/processed/usps/zone_chart.csv: one row per origin with a 1,000-character string,
   one zone digit per destination ZIP3 000-999 ("0" where the chart lists none).

The zone markers are dropped: "*" (same network distribution center, which matters only for
Parcel Select) and "+" (5-digit exceptions, listed separately; they are military APO/FPO
ranges). The effective date the tool reports is kept per origin.

Usage (about an hour for every origin at the default pace):

    uv run python -m data.collect.usps_zones                    # fetch what is missing, then build
    uv run python -m data.collect.usps_zones --limit 3          # try three origins
    uv run python -m data.collect.usps_zones --build-only       # rebuild the table from data/raw
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import hashlib
import json
import sys
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

from data.collect.announcements import fetch

DATA = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CHARTS = DATA / "raw" / "usps" / "zones" / "charts"
CHART_LIST = DATA / "raw" / "usps" / "zones" / "charts.csv"
TABLE = DATA / "processed" / "usps" / "zone_chart.csv"
URL = "https://postcalc.usps.com/DomesticZoneChart/GetZoneChart?zipCode3Digit={zip3}&shippingDate={month:02d}%2F{day:02d}%2F{year}"
SEED = "100"
LIST_COLUMNS = ["origin_zip3", "url", "sha256", "bytes", "effective_date", "fetched_on"]


def ranges(chart: dict) -> list[tuple[int, int, str]]:
    """(first ZIP3, last ZIP3, zone with markers) from the chart's columns, in order."""
    out = []
    for key in sorted(k for k in chart if k.startswith("Column")):
        for row in chart[key]:
            parts = row["ZipCodes"].split("---")
            first, last = int(parts[0]), int(parts[-1])
            out.append((first, last, row["Zone"].strip()))
    return out


def zone_string(chart: dict) -> str:
    """One digit per destination ZIP3 000-999; markers dropped, "0" where none is listed."""
    cells = ["0"] * 1000
    for first, last, zone in ranges(chart):
        digit = zone.rstrip("*+")
        if not digit.isdigit() or len(digit) != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"unexpected zone {zone!r}")
        for z in range(first, last + 1):
            cells[z] = digit
    return "".join(cells)


def origins_from(chart: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Every ZIP3 the chart lists as a destination: the prefixes that exist."""
    found = set()
    for first, last, _ in ranges(chart):
        found.update(range(first, last + 1))
    return [f"{z:03d}" for z in sorted(found)]


def read_list() -> dict[str, dict]:
    if not CHART_LIST.exists():
        return {}
    with CHART_LIST.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        return {r["origin_zip3"]: r for r in csv.DictReader(handle)}


def write_list(rows: dict[str, dict]) -> None:
    CHART_LIST.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with CHART_LIST.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=LIST_COLUMNS)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(rows[k] for k in sorted(rows))


def get_chart(zip3: str, on: date, listed: dict[str, dict]) -> dict | None:
    """The chart from disk when its checksum matches the list, else fetched and recorded."""
    path = CHARTS / f"{zip3}.json"
    row = listed.get(zip3)
    if path.exists() and row and hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == row["sha256"]:
        return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    url = URL.format(zip3=zip3, month=on.month, day=on.day, year=on.year)
    body = fetch(url)
    if body is None:
        return None
    chart = json.loads(body.decode("utf-8"))
    if chart.get("ZIPCodeError") or not any(k.startswith("Column") for k in chart):
        print(f"  {zip3}: no chart ({chart.get('ZIPCodeError') or 'empty'})")
        return None
    CHARTS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_bytes(body)
    listed[zip3] = {
        "origin_zip3": zip3, "url": url, "sha256": hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest(), "bytes": str(len(body)),
        "effective_date": chart.get("EffectiveDate", ""), "fetched_on": date.today().isoformat(),
    }
    return chart


def build(listed: dict[str, dict]) -> int:
    """Write the processed table from every chart on disk."""
    rows = []
    for zip3 in sorted(listed):
        path = CHARTS / f"{zip3}.json"
        if not path.exists():
            continue
        chart = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        rows.append({"origin_zip3": zip3, "effective_date": listed[zip3]["effective_date"],
                     "zones": zone_string(chart), "source_file": f"usps/zones/charts/{zip3}.json"})
    TABLE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with TABLE.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=["origin_zip3", "effective_date", "zones", "source_file"])
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(rows)
    return len(rows)


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, help="fetch at most this many origins")
    parser.add_argument("--build-only", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--date", type=date.fromisoformat, default=date.today(), help="shipping date asked for")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    listed = read_list()
    if not args.build_only:
        seed = get_chart(SEED, args.date, listed)
        if seed is None:
            print("the seed chart could not be fetched")
            return 1
        origins = origins_from(seed)
        print(f"{len(origins)} ZIP3 prefixes listed; {sum(1 for o in origins if o in listed)} already on disk")
        todo = [o for o in origins if o not in listed]
        if args.limit is not None:
            todo = todo[: args.limit]
        for i, zip3 in enumerate(todo, 1):
            get_chart(zip3, args.date, listed)
            if i % 25 == 0 or i == len(todo):
                write_list(listed)
                print(f"  {i}/{len(todo)} fetched")
        write_list(listed)
    print(f"wrote {build(listed)} origin rows to {TABLE.relative_to(DATA.parent)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

```

- `content`:

```
"""A point for every ZIP code, from the US Census Bureau's ZCTA Gazetteer (issue #9).

The distance between two ZIP codes estimates the UPS and FedEx zone (their zone charts cannot
be collected by script; see docs/DECISIONS.md). The Census Bureau publishes, for every ZIP Code
Tabulation Area (ZCTA, an approximation of a 5-digit ZIP's area), an interior point. This script

1. finds the latest national ZCTA Gazetteer file by rule: the newest year, counting down from
   the current one, whose file exists at the Census URL pattern;
2. downloads it once (politely, checksum recorded in data/raw/manifest.csv; the zip is not in
   git, data/fetch_raw.py restores it);
3. writes data/processed/shared/zip_points.csv: one row per ZCTA (zip5, lat, lon), and one row
   per 3-digit prefix (zip3) at the land-area-weighted centre of its ZCTAs. The prefix row is
   the fallback for ZIPs without a ZCTA (PO box and single-business ZIPs).

Usage:

    uv run python -m data.collect.zip_points
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import hashlib
import io
import sys
import zipfile
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

from data.collect.announcements import fetch

DATA = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
RAW = DATA / "raw"
MANIFEST = RAW / "manifest.csv"
TABLE = DATA / "processed" / "shared" / "zip_points.csv"
URL = "https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/maps-data/data/gazetteer/{year}_Gazetteer/{year}_Gaz_zcta_national.zip"
OLDEST = 2020


def latest_gazetteer() -> tuple[int, str, bytes] | None:
    for year in range(date.today().year, OLDEST - 1, -1):
        url = URL.format(year=year)
        body = fetch(url)
        if body and body[:2] == b"PK":
            return year, url, body
    return None


def rows_from(zip_bytes: bytes) -> list[dict]:
    """(zip5, lat, lon, land area) from the tab-separated file inside the zip."""
    with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(zip_bytes)) as archive:
        name = next(n for n in archive.namelist() if n.endswith(".txt"))
        text = archive.read(name).decode("utf-8-sig")
    reader = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text), delimiter="\t")
    reader.fieldnames = [f.strip() for f in reader.fieldnames or []]
    return [
        {"zip5": r["GEOID"].strip(), "lat": float(r["INTPTLAT"]), "lon": float(r["INTPTLONG"]), "aland": float(r["ALAND"])}
        for r in reader
    ]


def points(rows: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """ZCTA points plus land-area-weighted ZIP3 centres (plain mean when no land area)."""
    by3: dict[str, list[dict]] = defaultdict(list)
    for r in rows:
        by3[r["zip5"][:3]].append(r)
    out = [{"zip": r["zip5"], "kind": "zcta", "lat": f"{r['lat']:.6f}", "lon": f"{r['lon']:.6f}"} for r in rows]
    for zip3, members in sorted(by3.items()):
        weight = sum(m["aland"] for m in members) or len(members)
        lat = sum(m["lat"] * (m["aland"] or 1) for m in members) / weight
        lon = sum(m["lon"] * (m["aland"] or 1) for m in members) / weight
        out.append({"zip": zip3, "kind": "zip3", "lat": f"{lat:.6f}", "lon": f"{lon:.6f}"})
    return out


def record(year: int, url: str, body: bytes) -> str:
    path = f"shared/census/{year}_Gaz_zcta_national.zip"
    target = RAW / path
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    target.write_bytes(body)
    with MANIFEST.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        manifest = [r for r in csv.DictReader(handle) if r["path"] != path]
    fields = list(manifest[0].keys())
    manifest.append({
        "carrier": "shared", "year": str(year), "path": path, "url": url, "method": "direct",
        "sha256": hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest(), "bytes": str(len(body)), "in_git": "false",
        "content": f"US Census Bureau {year} ZCTA Gazetteer (national): interior point and land area per ZIP Code Tabulation Area",
    })
    with MANIFEST.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=fields)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(manifest)
    return path


def main() -> int:
    found = latest_gazetteer()
    if not found:
        print("no ZCTA Gazetteer file found")
        return 1
    year, url, body = found
    path = record(year, url, body)
    out = points(rows_from(body))
    TABLE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with TABLE.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=["zip", "kind", "lat", "lon"])
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(out)
    print(f"{path}: {sum(1 for r in out if r['kind'] == 'zcta')} ZCTAs, "
          f"{sum(1 for r in out if r['kind'] == 'zip3')} ZIP3 centres -> {TABLE.relative_to(DATA.parent)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

# ---- zone -----------------------------------------------------------------
def zone_for(tables: RateTables, carrier: str, distance_miles: float) -> int | None:
    """Band whose min_miles <= distance <= max_miles (empty max = open)."""
    bands = tables.zone_bands.get(carrier, [])
    for band in bands:
        if distance_miles >= band.min_miles and (
            band.max_miles is None or distance_miles <= band.max_miles
        ):
            return band.zone
    # Fractional distances between integer bands (e.g. 50.5): next band up.
    for band in bands:
        if distance_miles < band.min_miles:
            return band.zone
    return None


# ---- as_of ----------------------------------------------------------------

def weight_band(parcel: Parcel) -> str:
    for label, low, high in WEIGHT_BANDS:
        if low < parcel.weight_lb <= high:
            return label
    return WEIGHT_BANDS[-1][0]


def zone_band(tables: RateTables, parcel: Parcel) -> str:
    zone = zone_for(tables, SEGMENT_CARRIER, parcel.distance_miles)
    for label, low, high in ZONE_BANDS:
        if zone is not None and low <= zone <= high:
            return label
    return ZONE_BANDS[-1][0]

"""Zones from ZIP codes (issue #9): the real USPS chart, and distance between Census ZIP points
for UPS and FedEx (estimated)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from app.api import models as m
from app.engine.zip_zones import great_circle_miles


def _msgs(resp):
    return {tuple(e["loc"]): e["msg"] for e in resp.json()["detail"]}


def test_great_circle_miles():
    nyc, la = (40.7506, -73.9971), (34.0522, -118.2437)
    assert great_circle_miles(nyc, nyc) == 0
    assert 2440 <= great_circle_miles(nyc, la) <= 2460


def test_points_fall_back_to_the_zip3_centre(tables):
    z = tables.zip_zones
    exact = z.point("10001")
    assert exact is not None and exact.basis == "zcta"
    assert z.point("10001-1234") == exact
    # 10199 is a single-building ZIP (the former New York GPO) without a ZCTA of its own.
    fallback = z.point("10199")
    assert fallback is not None and fallback.basis == "zip3"
    assert z.point("00000") is None
    assert z.point("abc") is None


def test_usps_zone_from_the_chart(tables):
    z = tables.zip_zones
    assert z.usps_zone("10001", "90210") == 8
    assert z.usps_zone("10001", "10002") == 1
    assert z.usps_zone("10001", "00000") is None


def test_quote_from_zips_uses_the_usps_chart_and_estimates_ups_and_fedex(client):
    parcel = {"weight_lb": 2, "residential": True, "speed": "ground", "origin_zip": "10001", "destination_zip": "90210"}
    body = client.post("/api/quote", json={"parcel": parcel}).json()
    m.QuoteResponse.model_validate(body)
    by = {q["carrier"]: q for q in body["quotes"] if q["available"]}
    assert by["usps"]["zone"] == 8 and by["usps"]["zone_source"] == "usps_chart"
    assert by["ups"]["zone"] == 8 and by["ups"]["zone_source"] == "zip_distance"
    assert by["fedex"]["zone_source"] == "zip_distance"
    assert 2400 < body["distance_miles"] < 2500


def test_origin_zip_from_the_controls_and_typed_miles_still_work(client):
    parcel = {"weight_lb": 2, "residential": True, "speed": "ground", "destination_zip": "10002"}
    body = client.post("/api/quote", json={"parcel": parcel, "controls": {"origin_zip": "10001"}}).json()
    usps = next(q for q in body["quotes"] if q["carrier"] == "usps" and q["available"])
    assert usps["zone"] == 1 and usps["zone_source"] == "usps_chart"

    typed = {"weight_lb": 2, "residential": True, "speed": "ground", "distance_miles": 300}
    body = client.post("/api/quote", json={"parcel": typed}).json()
    assert {q["zone_source"] for q in body["quotes"] if q["available"]} == {"distance"}
    assert body["distance_miles"] == 300


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("parcel", "controls", "loc", "fragment"),
    [
        ({"weight_lb": 2, "residential": True, "speed": "ground"}, {}, ("body", "parcel"), "distance_miles or destination_zip"),
        ({"weight_lb": 2, "residential": True, "speed": "ground", "destination_zip": "90210"}, {},
         ("body", "parcel", "origin_zip"), "origin"),
        ({"weight_lb": 2, "residential": True, "speed": "ground", "destination_zip": "00000", "origin_zip": "10001"}, {},
         ("body", "parcel", "destination_zip"), "00000"),
        ({"weight_lb": 2, "residential": True, "speed": "ground", "destination_zip": "9021"}, {},
         ("body", "parcel", "destination_zip"), "5-digit"),
    ],
)
def test_zip_errors_name_the_field(client, parcel, controls, loc, fragment):
    msgs = _msgs(client.post("/api/quote", json={"parcel": parcel, "controls": controls}))
    assert loc in msgs, msgs
    assert fragment in msgs[loc]


def test_blended_with_zips(client):
    parcels = [
        {"weight_lb": 1, "residential": True, "speed": "ground", "destination_zip": "90210", "quantity": 2},
        {"weight_lb": 3, "residential": False, "speed": "ground", "distance_miles": 120},
    ]
    body = client.post("/api/blended", json={"parcels": parcels, "controls": {"origin_zip": "10001"}}).json()
    m.BlendedResponse.model_validate(body)
    assert body["parcels_considered"] == 3
    msgs = _msgs(client.post("/api/blended", json={"parcels": parcels[:1]}))
    assert ("body", "parcels", 0, "origin_zip") in msgs

"""Zones from ZIP codes (issue #9).

USPS: the real zone chart for the origin's 3-digit prefix (data/processed/usps/zone_chart.csv,
collected by data/collect/usps_zones.py). UPS and FedEx publish zone charts too, but not in a
form a script may collect, so their zone is estimated: the great-circle distance between the
two ZIPs' Census points (data/processed/zip_points.csv, data/collect/zip_points.py), then the
same distance bands as typed miles.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import math
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

EARTH_RADIUS_MILES = 3958.8
ZIP_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^(\d{5})(?:-\d{4})?$")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ZipPoint:
    lat: float
    lon: float
    basis: str  # "zcta": the ZIP's own Census area; "zip3": the centre of its 3-digit prefix


def great_circle_miles(a: tuple[float, float], b: tuple[float, float]) -> float:
    lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2 = map(math.radians, (*a, *b))
    h = math.sin((lat2 - lat1) / 2) ** 2 + math.cos(lat1) * math.cos(lat2) * math.sin((lon2 - lon1) / 2) ** 2
    return 2 * EARTH_RADIUS_MILES * math.asin(math.sqrt(h))


def zip5(value: str) -> str | None:
    match = ZIP_PATTERN.match(value.strip())
    return match.group(1) if match else None


@dataclass
class ZipZones:
    points: dict[str, tuple[float, float]]  # zip5 -> point
    centres: dict[str, tuple[float, float]]  # zip3 -> point
    usps_chart: dict[str, str]  # origin zip3 -> one zone digit per destination zip3 000-999
    usps_effective: str
    census_year: str

    def point(self, value: str) -> ZipPoint | None:
        code = zip5(value)
        if code is None:
            return None
        if code in self.points:
            return ZipPoint(*self.points[code], "zcta")
        if code[:3] in self.centres:
            return ZipPoint(*self.centres[code[:3]], "zip3")
        return None

    def miles(self, origin: str, destination: str) -> float | None:
        a, b = self.point(origin), self.point(destination)
        if a is None or b is None:
            return None
        return great_circle_miles((a.lat, a.lon), (b.lat, b.lon))

    def usps_zone(self, origin: str, destination: str) -> int | None:
        o, d = zip5(origin), zip5(destination)
        if o is None or d is None:
            return None
        row = self.usps_chart.get(o[:3])
        if row is None:
            return None
        digit = row[int(d[:3])]
        return int(digit) if digit != "0" else None


def load_zip_zones(data_dir: Path) -> ZipZones | None:
    """None when the ZIP tables are not there (the app then needs typed distances)."""
    points_path = data_dir / "zip_points.csv"
    chart_path = data_dir / "usps" / "zone_chart.csv"
    if not points_path.exists():
        return None
    points: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] = {}
    centres: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] = {}
    with points_path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for r in csv.DictReader(handle):
            target = points if r["kind"] == "zcta" else centres
            target[r["zip"]] = (float(r["lat"]), float(r["lon"]))
    chart: dict[str, str] = {}
    effective = ""
    if chart_path.exists():
        with chart_path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            for r in csv.DictReader(handle):
                chart[r["origin_zip3"]] = r["zones"]
                effective = r["effective_date"] or effective
    return ZipZones(points, centres, chart, effective, census_year="")
EOF

```
def _prefix(loc: tuple) -> str:
    parts = list(loc)
    if "parcels" in parts:
        i = parts.index("parcels")
        if i + 1 < len(parts) and isinstance(parts[i + 1], int):
            return f"Parcel {parts[i + 1] + 1}: "
    return ""


def friendly_message(error: dict) -> str:
    loc = tuple(error.get("loc", ()))
    kind = error.get("type", "")
    ctx = error.get("ctx") or {}
    field = _field(loc)
    messages = {
        "missing": f"{field} is required",
        "less_than_equal": f"{field} must be at most {_num(ctx.get('le'))}",
        "less_than": f"{field} must be less than {_num(ctx.get('lt'))}",
        "greater_than": f"{field} must be greater than {_num(ctx.get('gt'))}",
        "greater_than_equal": f"{field} must be at least {_num(ctx.get('ge'))}",
        "float_parsing": f"{field} must be a number",
        "float_type": f"{field} must be a number",
        "int_parsing": f"{field} must be a whole number",
        "int_type": f"{field} must be a whole number",
        "int_from_float": f"{field} must be a whole number",
        "bool_parsing": f"{field} must be true or false",
        "bool_type": f"{field} must be true or false",
        "literal_error": f"{field} must be one of {ctx.get('expected')}",
        "date_parsing": f"{field} must be a date like 2026-01-18",
        "date_from_datetime_parsing": f"{field} must be a date like 2026-01-18",
        "date_type": f"{field} must be a date like 2026-01-18",
        "too_short": f"{field} needs at least {ctx.get('min_length')} item(s)",
        "too_long": f"{field} can have at most {ctx.get('max_length')} items",
        "list_type": f"{field} must be a list",
        "model_type": f"{field} must be an object",
        "dict_type": f"{field} must be an object",
        "json_invalid": "the request body is not valid JSON",
        "extra_forbidden": f"{field} is not a known field",
    }
    if kind == "value_error":
        msg = str(error.get("msg", "")).removeprefix("Value error, ")
    else:
        msg = messages.get(kind, str(error.get("msg", "invalid value")))
    return _prefix(loc) + msg

**Tool call:** `Write` <sub>toolu_01RtnN7jVRwNaZ1PtDjndUcF</sub>

- `file_path`: `~/parcel-rates-label-redesign/data/collect/zone_accuracy.py`
- `content`:

```
"""How accurate is a zone estimated from the distance between two ZIP codes? (issue #9)

UPS and FedEx zones are estimated: great-circle miles between Census ZIP points, then the
distance bands in data/processed/zone_from_distance.csv. This script measures that estimate
against real zone charts and writes docs/data/ZONE_ACCURACY.md:

- USPS: the same estimate with the USPS bands, against the real USPS chart for every origin
  (data/processed/usps/zone_chart.csv), contiguous 48 states;
- UPS: the estimate with the UPS bands, against the UPS Ground zone charts that the Wayback
  Machine holds for 2026 (four origins; ups.com itself refuses scripted downloads). They are
  saved to data/raw/ups/zones/ with manifest rows.

Two ways to place a ZIP are measured: the centre of its 3-digit prefix (the charts are defined
per prefix) and, on a fixed random sample of 5-digit pairs, the ZIP's own Census point.

Usage:

    uv run python -m data.collect.zone_accuracy
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import hashlib
import io
import json
import random
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

from data.collect.announcements import CDX, fetch

DATA = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
ROOT = DATA.parent
PROCESSED = DATA / "processed"
RAW = DATA / "raw"
MANIFEST = RAW / "manifest.csv"
REPORT = ROOT / "docs" / "data" / "ZONE_ACCURACY.md"
UPS_PREFIX = "www.ups.com/media/us/currentrates/zone-csv/"
UPS_FROM = "2026"
SAMPLE_PAIRS = 200_000
SEED = 20261023

# ZIP3 prefixes outside the contiguous 48 states (PR, VI, military, HI, Pacific, AK).
NOT_CONTIGUOUS = {*range(6, 10), *range(90, 100), 340, *range(962, 970), *range(995, 1000)}


def great_circle_miles(a, b) -> float:
    import math

    lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2 = map(math.radians, (*a, *b))
    h = math.sin((lat2 - lat1) / 2) ** 2 + math.cos(lat1) * math.cos(lat2) * math.sin((lon2 - lon1) / 2) ** 2
    return 2 * 3958.8 * math.asin(math.sqrt(h))


def bands(carrier: str) -> list[tuple[int, float, float | None]]:
    with (PROCESSED / "zone_from_distance.csv").open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        rows = [r for r in csv.DictReader(handle) if r["carrier"] == carrier]
    return sorted(
        (int(r["zone"]), float(r["min_miles"]), float(r["max_miles"]) if r["max_miles"] else None) for r in rows
    )


def zone_for(table, miles: float) -> int | None:
    """Same rule as backend/app/engine/rules.py zone_for."""
    for zone, low, high in table:
        if miles >= low and (high is None or miles <= high):
            return zone
    for zone, low, _ in table:
        if miles < low:
            return zone
    return None


def load_points() -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[float, float]], dict[str, tuple[float, float]]]:
    zcta, centres = {}, {}
    with (PROCESSED / "zip_points.csv").open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for r in csv.DictReader(handle):
            (zcta if r["kind"] == "zcta" else centres)[r["zip"]] = (float(r["lat"]), float(r["lon"]))
    return zcta, centres


def load_usps_chart() -> dict[str, str]:
    with (PROCESSED / "usps" / "zone_chart.csv").open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        return {r["origin_zip3"]: r["zones"] for r in csv.DictReader(handle)}


class Tally:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.diff: Counter[int] = Counter()

    def add(self, real: int, estimate: int | None) -> None:
        if estimate is not None:
            self.diff[estimate - real] += 1

    @property
    def n(self) -> int:
        return sum(self.diff.values())

    def share(self, pred) -> str:
        return f"{sum(v for k, v in self.diff.items() if pred(k)) / self.n:.1%}" if self.n else "–"

    def row(self, label: str) -> str:
        return (f"| {label} | {self.n:,} | {self.share(lambda d: d == 0)} | {self.share(lambda d: abs(d) == 1)} | "
                f"{self.share(lambda d: abs(d) >= 2)} | {self.share(lambda d: d < 0)} | {self.share(lambda d: d > 0)} |")


def contiguous(zip3: str) -> bool:
    return int(zip3) not in NOT_CONTIGUOUS


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- USPS
def usps_tallies(chart, zcta, centres) -> tuple[Tally, Tally]:
    usps = bands("usps")
    by_prefix, by_zip = Tally(), Tally()
    origins = [o for o in chart if contiguous(o) and o in centres]
    for o in origins:
        row = chart[o]
        for d in range(1000):
            d3 = f"{d:03d}"
            real = row[d]
            if real == "0" or not contiguous(d3) or d3 not in centres:
                continue
            by_prefix.add(int(real), zone_for(usps, great_circle_miles(centres[o], centres[d3])))
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    zips = [z for z in zcta if contiguous(z[:3]) and z[:3] in chart]
    for _ in range(SAMPLE_PAIRS):
        a, b = rng.choice(zips), rng.choice(zips)
        real = chart[a[:3]][int(b[:3])]
        if real != "0":
            by_zip.add(int(real), zone_for(usps, great_circle_miles(zcta[a], zcta[b])))
    return by_prefix, by_zip


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- UPS
def ups_captures() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """(origin zip3, id_ URL) for the latest 2026 capture of each archived UPS zone chart."""
    query = f"{CDX}?url={UPS_PREFIX}&matchType=prefix&output=json&fl=timestamp,original&filter=statuscode:200&from={UPS_FROM}"
    body = fetch(query)
    latest: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {}
    for timestamp, original in json.loads(body.decode("utf-8") or "[]")[1:] if body else []:
        name = original.rsplit("/", 1)[-1].split("?")[0]
        zip3 = name.split(".")[0]
        if zip3.isdigit() and len(zip3) == 3 and (zip3 not in latest or timestamp > latest[zip3][0]):
            latest[zip3] = (timestamp, original)
    return [(z, f"https://web.archive.org/web/{t}id_/{u}") for z, (t, u) in sorted(latest.items())]


def ups_chart(body: bytes) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Destination ZIP3 -> UPS Ground zone (2-8) from a UPS zone workbook."""
    import openpyxl

    sheet = openpyxl.load_workbook(io.BytesIO(body), read_only=True).worksheets[0]
    out: dict[str, int] = {}
    for row in sheet.iter_rows(values_only=True):
        dest, ground = (str(row[0] or "").strip(), str(row[1] or "").strip()) if len(row) > 1 else ("", "")
        if not ground.isdigit() or not 2 <= int(ground) <= 8:
            continue  # headers, '-' and the 044-046 zones of Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico
        parts = dest.split("-")
        if all(p.isdigit() and len(p) == 3 for p in parts):
            for d in range(int(parts[0]), int(parts[-1]) + 1):
                out[f"{d:03d}"] = int(ground)
    return out


def save_raw(path: str, url: str, body: bytes) -> None:
    target = RAW / path
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    target.write_bytes(body)
    with MANIFEST.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        manifest = [r for r in csv.DictReader(handle) if r["path"] != path]
    fields = list(manifest[0].keys())
    manifest.append({"carrier": "ups", "year": "2026", "path": path, "url": url, "method": "wayback",
                     "sha256": hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest(), "bytes": str(len(body)), "in_git": "true",
                     "content": "UPS zone chart (Ground and air zones by destination ZIP3) for one origin, Wayback capture; "
                                "used only to measure the distance-based zone estimate"})
    with MANIFEST.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=fields)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(manifest)


def ups_tallies(zcta, centres) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, Tally, Tally]], list[str]]:
    ups = bands("ups")
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    out, sources = [], []
    for zip3, url in ups_captures():
        body = fetch(url)
        if not body or body[:2] != b"PK":
            continue
        path = f"ups/zones/{zip3}_{url.split('/web/')[1][:8]}.xlsx"
        save_raw(path, url, body)
        sources.append(f"`data/raw/{path}`")
        real = ups_chart(body)
        by_prefix, by_zip = Tally(), Tally()
        for d3, zone in real.items():
            if contiguous(d3) and d3 in centres and zip3 in centres:
                by_prefix.add(zone, zone_for(ups, great_circle_miles(centres[zip3], centres[d3])))
        origins = [z for z in zcta if z[:3] == zip3]
        dests = [z for z in zcta if z[:3] in real and contiguous(z[:3])]
        for _ in range(SAMPLE_PAIRS // 20):
            a, b = rng.choice(origins), rng.choice(dests)
            by_zip.add(real[b[:3]], zone_for(ups, great_circle_miles(zcta[a], zcta[b])))
        out.append((zip3, by_prefix, by_zip))
    return out, sources


HEADER = "| Measured | Pairs | Exact | Off by one | Off by two or more | Estimate lower | Estimate higher |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"


def main() -> int:
    zcta, centres = load_points()
    chart = load_usps_chart()
    usps_prefix, usps_zip = usps_tallies(chart, zcta, centres)
    ups, sources = ups_tallies(zcta, centres)
    lines = [
        "# Zone estimate from ZIP distance: measured accuracy",
        "",
        "Generated by `uv run python -m data.collect.zone_accuracy` (issue #9). UPS and FedEx zones",
        "are estimated from the great-circle distance between two ZIP codes' Census points and the",
        "distance bands in `data/processed/zone_from_distance.csv`; this measures that estimate",
        "against real charts, contiguous 48 states. \"Lower\" means the estimate is a lower zone than",
        "the chart (a cheaper price than the carrier would charge).",
        "",
        f"## USPS: the same estimate against the real USPS chart ({len(chart)} origin prefixes)",
        "",
        HEADER,

        "distance estimate gets where the real answer is known.",
        "",
        f"## UPS: against the UPS Ground charts archived for 2026 ({len(ups)} origins)",
        "",
        HEADER,
    ]
    total_prefix, total_zip = Tally(), Tally()
    for zip3, by_prefix, by_zip in ups:
        lines.append(by_prefix.row(f"origin {zip3}, ZIP3 centres"))
        lines.append(by_zip.row(f"origin {zip3}, 5-digit points (sample)"))
        total_prefix.diff.update(by_prefix.diff)
        total_zip.diff.update(by_zip.diff)
    lines += [total_prefix.row("all origins, ZIP3 centres"), total_zip.row("all origins, 5-digit points (sample)"), ""]
    lines += ["Sources: " + ", ".join(sources) + "." if sources else "No archived UPS chart could be fetched.", ""]
    REPORT.write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
    print("\n".join(lines))
    return 0

    sys.exit(main())

import type { DeliveryArea, Parcel, Tier } from "../../api/types";

/** The quote form as the user types it: strings, so half-typed numbers survive. */
export interface Draft {
  lb: string;
  oz: string;
  length: string;
  width: string;
  height: string;
  distance: string;
  residential: boolean;
  speed: Tier;
  area: DeliveryArea;
  nonstandard: boolean;
}

export const DEFAULT_DRAFT: Draft = {
  lb: "3",
  oz: "",
  length: "12",
  width: "10",
  height: "6",
  distance: "600",
  residential: true,
  speed: "ground",
  area: "none",
  nonstandard: false,
};

/** A number as typed: "1,5" is read as 1.5 (decimal comma); thousands separators are not expected here. */
export const parseNum = (s: string): number | null => {
  const t = s.trim().replace(",", ".");
  if (t === "") return null;
  const n = Number(t);
  return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : NaN;
};

/** Total weight in lb from the lb and oz boxes; null when neither is filled, NaN when garbled. */
export function draftWeight(d: Draft): number | null {
  const lb = parseNum(d.lb);
  const oz = parseNum(d.oz);
  if (lb === null && oz === null) return null;
  if (Number.isNaN(lb) || Number.isNaN(oz)) return NaN;
  return Math.round(((lb ?? 0) + (oz ?? 0) / 16) * 10000) / 10000;
}

export type LocalErrors = Partial<Record<"weight" | "dims" | "distance", string>>;

/**
 * Turn the draft into a request parcel. Only shape problems are caught here (empty, not a
 * number, two of three dimensions); ranges are left to the server so its 422 messages show.
 */
export function draftToParcel(d: Draft): { parcel: Parcel; errors: null } | { parcel: null; errors: LocalErrors } {
  const errors: LocalErrors = {};
  const weight = draftWeight(d);
  if (weight === null) errors.weight = "Enter the weight.";
  else if (Number.isNaN(weight)) errors.weight = "Weight must be a number.";
  const dims = [d.length, d.width, d.height].map(parseNum);
  const filled = dims.filter((x) => x !== null).length;
  if (dims.some((x) => Number.isNaN(x))) errors.dims = "Dimensions must be numbers.";
  else if (filled > 0 && filled < 3) errors.dims = "Give all three dimensions, or leave all three empty.";
  const distance = parseNum(d.distance);
  if (distance === null) errors.distance = "Enter the distance.";
  else if (Number.isNaN(distance)) errors.distance = "Distance must be a number.";
  if (Object.keys(errors).length > 0) return { parcel: null, errors };
  const parcel: Parcel = {
    weight_lb: weight!,
    distance_miles: distance!,
    residential: d.residential,
    speed: d.speed,
    delivery_area: d.area,
    nonstandard_packaging: d.nonstandard,
    ...(filled === 3 ? { length_in: dims[0]!, width_in: dims[1]!, height_in: dims[2]! } : {}),
  };
  return { parcel, errors: null };
}

const str = (n: number | null | undefined) => (n === null || n === undefined ? "" : String(n));

export function draftFromParcel(p: Parcel): Draft {

  });

/** `zoneBands`: the zone bands from /api/meta; the USPS ones bucket the distances. */
export function summarize(parcels: Parcel[], zoneBands?: ZoneBand[]): ParcelSummary {
  const zones = uspsZones(zoneBands);
  const total = parcels.reduce((s, p) => s + qty(p), 0);
  const share = (pred: (p: Parcel) => boolean) =>
    total ? parcels.filter(pred).reduce((s, p) => s + qty(p), 0) / total : 0;
  const byTier = Object.fromEntries(TIERS.map((t) => [t, share((p) => p.speed === t)])) as Record<Tier, number>;
  return {
    rows: parcels.length,
    parcels: total,
    residentialShare: share((p) => p.residential),
    byTier,
    weight: buckets(parcels, WEIGHT_BANDS, (p) => weightBand(p.weight_lb), total),
    distance: buckets(
      parcels,
      zones.map(zoneLabel),
      (p) => zoneLabel(zoneForDistance(p.distance_miles, zones)),
      total,
      (_l, i) => zoneRange(zones[i]!),
    ),
    withOwnPrice: parcels.filter((p) => p.price_charged !== undefined).reduce((s, p) => s + qty(p), 0),
    meanWeightLb: total ? parcels.reduce((s, p) => s + p.weight_lb * qty(p), 0) / total : 0,
  };
}

import { useId, type ReactNode } from "react";
import type { Carrier, DeliveryArea, Parcel, Tier } from "../../api/types";
import { CARRIERS, TIERS } from "../../api/types";
import { draftFromParcel, draftWeight, type Draft } from "./draft";
import type { FormField } from "./quoteModel";
import { CARRIER_NAME } from "../../lib/carriers";
import { TIER_NAME } from "../../lib/format";

export interface QuoteFormProps {
  draft: Draft;
  onChange: (next: Draft) => void;
  /** Messages per field: local shape checks and the server's 422 messages. */
  errors: Partial<Record<FormField, string[]>>;
  /** Zone per carrier from the last quote, shown under the distance. */
  zones: Partial<Record<Carrier, number>> | null;
  parcels: Parcel[] | null;
}

const AREA_LABEL: Record<DeliveryArea, string> = {
  none: "Standard area",
  das: "Remote (DAS)",
  extended: "Extended remote",
};

function zoneLine(zones: Partial<Record<Carrier, number>>): string | null {
  const entries = CARRIERS.filter((c) => zones[c] !== undefined).map((c) => [c, zones[c]!] as const);
  if (entries.length === 0) return null;
  const distinct = new Set(entries.map(([, z]) => z));
  if (distinct.size === 1) return `Zone ${entries[0]![1]}${entries.length > 1 ? " for every carrier" : ` (${CARRIER_NAME[entries[0]![0]]})`}`;
  return entries.map(([c, z]) => `${CARRIER_NAME[c]} zone ${z}`).join(" · ");
}

function parcelLabel(p: Parcel, i: number): string {
  const dims = p.length_in ? ` · ${p.length_in}×${p.width_in}×${p.height_in} in` : "";
  return `#${i + 1}: ${p.weight_lb} lb${dims} · ${p.distance_miles} mi · ${p.residential ? "home" : "business"} · ${TIER_NAME[p.speed]}`;
}

const MAX_PICKS = 300;

function Errors({ id, messages }: { id: string; messages: string[] | undefined }) {
  if (!messages || messages.length === 0) return null;
  return (
    <p id={id} className="control__error qf__error">
      {messages.join(" ")}
    </p>
  );
}

function Field({ label, htmlFor, children, hint }: { label: string; htmlFor?: string; children: ReactNode; hint?: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <div className="qf__field">
      <label className="control__label" htmlFor={htmlFor}>
        {label}
      </label>
      {children}
      {hint}
    </div>
  );
}

export function QuoteForm({ draft, onChange, errors, zones, parcels }: QuoteFormProps) {
  const uid = useId();
  const id = (s: string) => `${uid}-${s}`;

  const zoneText = zones ? zoneLine(zones) : null;

text shown in the UI footer. Shape: `MetaResponse` in `backend/app/api/models.py`.

### GET /api/sample-parcels
The bundled illustrative parcel mix as `Parcel[]`, with a `description`.

### POST /api/quote  (question 1)
Request `{ parcel: Parcel, controls: Controls }`. Response
`{ quotes: Quote[], cheapest_by_tier: Record<Tier, {carrier, service_id, total}> }`,
quotes sorted by total within the requested tier first, then the other tiers
(unavailable quotes last within a tier). Only carriers that publish the
requested year are quoted (2027 is FedEx only). A tier with no available
service maps to `null` in `cheapest_by_tier`.

  section; assumptions sit in a quiet side rail. See
  [frontend/DESIGN.md](frontend/DESIGN.md).

## Known limitations

- List prices only: a shipper with a negotiated contract pays less.
- Zones are estimated from distance bands, not looked up from ZIP code pairs.
- The UPS fuel surcharge default is a proxy taken from FedEx's published
  history (no UPS history is retrievable); the slider overrides it.
- UPS announced increases come from trade press, not from UPS itself.
- UPS peak (demand) surcharge documents for the 2025-26 and 2026-27 seasons
  are not in the sources, so UPS 2025 and 2026 peak quotes carry no peak
  charges.
- FedEx 2027 surcharges are incomplete (only the Home Delivery residential
  charge and January peak rows), so 2027 totals understate surcharges.
- Peak surcharges are a toggle that prices on December 10 of the year, not by
  ship date.
- UPS and FedEx bill a large or oversize package at a minimum of 90 lb. The
  minimum is modelled (issue #18), but actual weight is still capped at 70 lb;
  parcels whose dimensional weight is 71–150 lb are priced from the carriers'
  tables.
- Weight is capped at 70 lb, the USPS maximum. Alaska and Hawaii are out of
  scope.
- UPS 2024 and 2026 use the mid-year revision of the Daily Rates guide,
  because the December original could not be retrieved.

The same list is returned by `GET /api/meta` and shown in the app.

## What I would improve next

Open issues in the repository, in rough priority order:

- #18 model the 90 lb minimum billable weight for large and oversize packages.
- #14 capture the UPS 2025-26 and 2026-27 demand surcharge documents.
- #9 real ZIP-to-ZIP zones instead of distance bands.
- #10 per-parcel price column and order-value shipping rules (free shipping
  over a threshold).

```
"""ZIP data for zones (issue #9): the collectors' rules on small inline inputs, and the shape of
the processed tables they write."""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv

from data.collect import usps_zones, zip_points
from data.pipeline.common import processed_path

CHART = {
    "ZIPCodeError": "",
    "EffectiveDate": "October 1, 2026",
    "Column0": [
        {"ZipCodes": "005", "Zone": "1*", "MailService": ""},
        {"ZipCodes": "006---009", "Zone": "7", "MailService": ""},
        {"ZipCodes": "010---013", "Zone": "2+", "MailService": ""},
    ],
    "Column1": [{"ZipCodes": "96700", "Zone": "8", "MailService": ""}],
    "Zip5Digit": [{"ZipCodes": "09000---09999", "Zone": "5", "MailService": "Priority Mail service"}],
}


def test_zone_string_drops_markers_and_five_digit_entries():
    zones = usps_zones.zone_string(CHART)
    assert len(zones) == 1000
    assert zones[5] == "1" and zones[6:10] == "7777" and zones[10:14] == "2222"
    assert zones[967] == "0" and zones[0] == "0"
    assert usps_zones.origins_from(CHART) == ["005", "006", "007", "008", "009", "010", "011", "012", "013"]


def test_zip3_centre_is_land_weighted():
    rows = [
        {"zip5": "10001", "lat": 40.0, "lon": -74.0, "aland": 3.0},
        {"zip5": "10002", "lat": 42.0, "lon": -72.0, "aland": 1.0},
    ]
    out = {r["zip"]: r for r in zip_points.points(rows)}
    assert out["10001"]["kind"] == "zcta"
    assert (out["100"]["kind"], out["100"]["lat"], out["100"]["lon"]) == ("zip3", "40.500000", "-73.500000")


def test_processed_zone_chart_and_points_agree():
    with processed_path("usps", "zone_chart").open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        chart = list(csv.DictReader(handle))
    with processed_path("shared", "zip_points").open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        points = list(csv.DictReader(handle))
    assert chart, "no USPS zone chart rows"
    for row in chart:
        assert len(row["zones"]) == 1000 and set(row["zones"]) <= set("0123456789"), row["origin_zip3"]
        assert row["effective_date"]
    centres = {r["zip"] for r in points if r["kind"] == "zip3"}
    contiguous = [r["origin_zip3"] for r in chart if r["origin_zip3"] in centres]
    assert len(contiguous) >= 0.9 * len(chart)  # most chart origins have a Census centre
    assert sum(1 for r in points if r["kind"] == "zcta") > 30_000

```

# Zone estimate from ZIP distance: measured accuracy

distance bands in `data/processed/zone_from_distance.csv`; this measures that estimate

#9 is done on branch `issue-9-zip-zones`, in seven commits, not pushed yet. Zones now come from ZIP codes: USPS from its real zone chart, UPS and FedEx from an estimate whose accuracy I measured before shipping.

**Data:**
- **USPS:** zone charts for all 914 origin prefixes, effective 1 October 2026. Collection took about 75 minutes, politely and resumably. The other 16 listed prefixes, including military APO/FPO 090–099, have no chart in the USPS tool. The processed table is 940 KB; the raw charts stay out of git and are checked against a checksum list.
- **ZIP points:** the US Census 2026 ZIP-area file, 33,791 areas, plus a land-weighted centre per 3-digit prefix for ZIPs without an area, such as PO boxes.
- **Accuracy check:** the five 2026 UPS zone charts the Wayback Machine holds are saved and used to measure the UPS estimate.

**Measured accuracy** (`docs/data/ZONE_ACCURACY.md`), never off by two zones:

| Estimate | Against | Exact |
|---|---|---|
| Distance between prefix centres | USPS chart, 781,456 prefix pairs | **97.4%** |
| Distance between prefix centres | UPS charts, 5 origins | **90.8%** |
| Distance between each ZIP's own point | USPS / UPS | 92.3% / 90.4% |
| USPS chart zone read as a UPS zone | UPS charts | 89.8% |

**Two changes to the plan I described, both driven by the measurements:**
- **Prefix centres instead of 5-digit points.** I had planned to use each ZIP's own point and fall back to the prefix centre; the prefix centres measured clearly better.
- **The UPS estimate leans one zone high.** When it's wrong, it's usually one zone too high (7.4% of lanes, against 1.7% too low), so estimated UPS prices lean slightly high.

**App:**
- **Ship from ZIP:** a new assumption, beside the year.
- **Q1:** a "Destination ZIP" field. When it's filled, the miles box is disabled and shows the distance between the ZIP areas. The zone line reads, for example, "USPS zone 8 (zone chart) · UPS zone 8 (estimated) · FedEx zone 8 (estimated)".
- **CSV:** accepts `destination_zip` and `origin_zip`, each row needing `distance_miles` or `destination_zip`. If a spreadsheet dropped a ZIP's leading zeros, they're restored with a warning.
- **API:** each quote reports `zone_source` (USPS chart, estimated from the ZIPs, or typed miles), and `/api/meta` reports what ZIP data the server has.
- **Unchanged:** typed miles still work, and Q2's map is still distance-based.

**Checks:**
- Backend tests, data tests and ruff pass.
- Frontend: 210 of 210 unit tests pass, plus typecheck and the build.
- e2e: 63 passed, 1 skipped (the phone-only test), including a new ZIP test on desktop and phone that I fixed after it flaked once.
- axe: no findings on all 24 runs, with a ship-from ZIP and a destination ZIP in use.
- The screenshots, README images, API examples and fixtures are regenerated, and API.md, SCHEMA.md, the README, DESIGN.md and DECISIONS.md are updated. The README's "What I would improve next" list no longer names #9, #10 and #11 (now done) or the long-closed #18, and now suggests real UPS and FedEx zones through their official APIs.

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

const DARK = "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)";

/** Resolve CSS custom properties to concrete colours (for Recharts); re-resolves when the colour scheme flips. */
export function useCssColors<K extends string>(vars: Record<K, string>): Record<K, string> {
  const read = () => {
    const style = typeof document === "undefined" ? null : getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
    const out = {} as Record<K, string>;
    for (const k in vars) out[k] = style?.getPropertyValue(vars[k]).trim() || "currentColor";
    return out;
  };
  const [colors, setColors] = useState(read);
  const key = JSON.stringify(vars);
  useEffect(() => {
    setColors(read());
    const mq = typeof window !== "undefined" && window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia(DARK) : null;
    if (!mq) return;
    const onChange = () => setColors(read());
    mq.addEventListener?.("change", onChange);
    return () => mq.removeEventListener?.("change", onChange);
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [key]);
  return colors;
}

cd ~/parcel-rates-label-redesign/frontend && cat > public/theme.js <<'EOF'
/* Sets data-theme on <html> before the first paint: the owner's saved choice, else the system
   setting (followed live until a choice is saved). External, not inline, because the CSP
   allows only same-origin scripts. src/lib/theme.ts saves the choice under the same key. */
(function () {
  var KEY = "parcel-rates-theme";
  var root = document.documentElement;
  var system = window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)") : null;
  function saved() {
    try {
      var v = window.localStorage.getItem(KEY);
      return v === "light" || v === "dark" ? v : null;
    } catch (e) {
      return null;
    }
  }
  function apply() {
    root.setAttribute("data-theme", saved() || (system && system.matches ? "dark" : "light"));
  }
  apply();
  if (system && system.addEventListener) system.addEventListener("change", function () {
    if (!saved()) apply();
  });
})();
EOF

cd ~/parcel-rates-label-redesign/frontend/src && cat > lib/theme.ts <<'EOF'
/** Light or dark, as set on <html data-theme> by public/theme.js (saved choice or system). */
export type Theme = "light" | "dark";

/** Same key as public/theme.js. */
export const THEME_KEY = "parcel-rates-theme";

export function currentTheme(): Theme {
  return document.documentElement.getAttribute("data-theme") === "dark" ? "dark" : "light";
}

/** Apply a theme now and remember it, so it wins over the system setting from then on. */
export function setTheme(theme: Theme): void {
  document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", theme);
  try {
    window.localStorage.setItem(THEME_KEY, theme);
  } catch {
    // Private windows and blocked storage: the choice holds for this page only.
  }
}
EOF
cat > components/ThemeToggle.tsx <<'EOF'
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { currentTheme, setTheme, type Theme } from "../lib/theme";

/** "Dark mode" on or off; starts from the system setting until the owner chooses. */
export function ThemeToggle() {
  const [theme, setLocal] = useState<Theme>(currentTheme);
  // public/theme.js follows the system until a choice is saved; mirror its changes.
  useEffect(() => {
    const observer = new MutationObserver(() => setLocal(currentTheme()));
    observer.observe(document.documentElement, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ["data-theme"] });
    return () => observer.disconnect();
  }, []);
  const dark = theme === "dark";
  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      className="theme-toggle"
      aria-pressed={dark}
      onClick={() => {
        const next: Theme = dark ? "light" : "dark";
        setTheme(next);
        setLocal(next);
      }}
    >
      <span className="theme-toggle__box" aria-hidden="true" />
      Dark mode
    </button>
  );
}
EOF
cat > hooks/useCssColors.ts <<'EOF'
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

/** Resolve CSS custom properties to concrete colours (for Recharts); re-resolves when the theme
 *  flips (data-theme on <html>, set by public/theme.js and the masthead toggle). */
export function useCssColors<K extends string>(vars: Record<K, string>): Record<K, string> {
  const read = () => {
    const style = typeof document === "undefined" ? null : getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
    const out = {} as Record<K, string>;
    for (const k in vars) out[k] = style?.getPropertyValue(vars[k]).trim() || "currentColor";
    return out;
  };
  const [colors, setColors] = useState(read);
  const key = JSON.stringify(vars);
  useEffect(() => {
    setColors(read());
    if (typeof MutationObserver === "undefined") return;
    const observer = new MutationObserver(() => setColors(read()));
    observer.observe(document.documentElement, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ["data-theme"] });
    return () => observer.disconnect();
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [key]);
  return colors;
}
EOF

import { afterEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { render, screen } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import { ThemeToggle } from "./ThemeToggle";
import { THEME_KEY } from "../lib/theme";

afterEach(() => {
  document.documentElement.removeAttribute("data-theme");
  window.localStorage.clear();
});

describe("ThemeToggle", () => {
  it("starts from the theme already set and switches and remembers it", async () => {
    document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    render(<ThemeToggle />);
    const toggle = screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Dark mode" });
    expect(toggle).toHaveAttribute("aria-pressed", "false");
    await userEvent.click(toggle);
    expect(document.documentElement).toHaveAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    expect(window.localStorage.getItem(THEME_KEY)).toBe("dark");
    expect(toggle).toHaveAttribute("aria-pressed", "true");
    await userEvent.click(toggle);
    expect(document.documentElement).toHaveAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    expect(window.localStorage.getItem(THEME_KEY)).toBe("light");
  });

  it("follows a theme change made elsewhere (the system, before a choice is saved)", async () => {
    document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    render(<ThemeToggle />);
    document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    expect(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Dark mode", pressed: true })).toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});
EOF
cat > e2e/theme.spec.ts <<'EOF'
import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";
import { openApp } from "./helpers";

test.describe("Light and dark mode", () => {
  test("follows the system, then the owner's choice, which survives a reload", async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: "dark" });
    await openApp(page);
    const html = page.locator("html");
    const toggle = page.getByRole("button", { name: "Dark mode" });
    await expect(html).toHaveAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    await expect(toggle).toHaveAttribute("aria-pressed", "true");
    const darkPaper = await page.evaluate(() => getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor);

    await toggle.click();
    await expect(html).toHaveAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    await expect(toggle).toHaveAttribute("aria-pressed", "false");
    expect(await page.evaluate(() => getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor)).not.toBe(darkPaper);

    await openApp(page);
    await expect(html).toHaveAttribute("data-theme", "light"); // the saved choice beats the dark system
  });
});
EOF

I've added a "Dark mode" toggle to the masthead. It's committed on branch `theme-toggle` (`321d57b`), not pushed yet.

**How it works:**
- **Default:** the theme follows your system setting, live, until you press the toggle.
- **Pressing it:** switches immediately, and the choice is saved in the browser, so it survives reloads and wins over the system setting.
- **Look:** a small box labelled "Dark mode", filled when on, at the right of the masthead. It sits beside the title on phones.
- **No flash on load:** a small script in the page head sets the theme before the first paint. It's a separate file because the site's security policy forbids inline scripts. The production build includes it, and the existing policy allows it without changes.
- **Charts:** they redraw in the new colours when you switch.

**Checks:** 212 of 212 unit tests pass, including two new ones for the toggle. e2e: 65 passed, 1 skipped (the phone-only test), including a new test for following the system, switching, and keeping the choice after a reload. axe found nothing on all 24 runs. Screenshots, the README images and DESIGN.md are updated.

One limit: once you've chosen, there's no button to go back to following the system setting; clearing the site's storage does it. A third "Auto" state would fix that, if you want it.

# Agent session log

Every Claude Code session run in this repository is exported here as Markdown
when the session ends, by the `SessionEnd` hook configured in
`.claude/settings.json` (`.claude/hooks/export-session.sh`).

- One file per session, named `<session-id>.md`. A resumed session keeps its
  id, so it overwrites its own earlier export.
- The export contains the full main transcript (user prompts, assistant text,
  thinking, tool calls and tool results) followed by one section per subagent
  transcript spawned from that session.
- The hook commits the exported file on its own (`docs(agent-log): export
  session <id>`), touching nothing else in the index.

To export the current session by hand:

```sh
printf '{"session_id":"%s","transcript_path":"%s","cwd":"%s","reason":"manual"}' \
  "$SID" "$HOME/.claude/projects/<encoded-project-path>/$SID.jsonl" "$PWD" \
  | .claude/hooks/export-session.sh
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SessionEnd hook: export the session transcript (plus any subagent transcripts)
# to docs/agent-log/<session-id>.md and commit that file.
#
# Reads the hook payload on stdin:
#   {"session_id": "...", "transcript_path": "...", "cwd": "...", "reason": "..."}
# Can also be run by hand with the same JSON on stdin.
#
# Dependencies: bash, jq, git.
set -euo pipefail

here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
filter="$here/transcript-to-md.jq"

input=$(cat)
sid=$(jq -r '.session_id // empty' <<<"$input")
tp=$(jq -r '.transcript_path // empty' <<<"$input")
reason=$(jq -r '.reason // "manual"' <<<"$input")
cwd=$(jq -r '.cwd // empty' <<<"$input")
root=$(git -C "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-${cwd:-$here}}" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || root=$(git -C "$here" rev-parse --show-toplevel)

if [[ -z "$sid" || -z "$tp" ]]; then
  echo "export-session: missing session_id or transcript_path in hook input" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [[ ! -s "$tp" ]]; then
  echo "export-session: transcript $tp missing or empty, nothing to export" >&2
  exit 0
fi

outdir="$root/docs/agent-log"
out="$outdir/$sid.md"
mkdir -p "$outdir"
trap 'rm -f "$out.tmp"' EXIT

render() { # render <heading-prefix> ; records on stdin
  jq -rs --arg h "$1" -f "$filter"
}

meta() { # meta <jq expr> over the main transcript
  jq -rs "$1" "$tp"
}

{
  echo "# Agent session $sid"
  echo
  echo "| | |"
  echo "|---|---|"
  echo "| Project | \`$(meta '[.[] | .cwd // empty] | first // ""')\` |"
  echo "| Branch | \`$(meta '[.[] | .gitBranch // empty] | first // ""')\` |"
  echo "| Claude Code | $(meta '[.[] | .version // empty] | first // ""') |"
  echo "| Started | $(meta '[.[] | .timestamp // empty] | min // ""') |"
  echo "| Last record | $(meta '[.[] | .timestamp // empty] | max // ""') |"
  echo "| Exported | $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) (reason: $reason) |"
  echo "| Source | \`$tp\` |"
  echo
  jq -c 'select(.isSidechain != true)' "$tp" | render "##"

  # Subagent transcripts, newer layout: <transcript-dir>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl
  subdir="${tp%.jsonl}/subagents"
  if [[ -d "$subdir" ]]; then
    for f in "$subdir"/*.jsonl; do
      [[ -s "$f" ]] || continue
      name=$(basename "$f" .jsonl)
      meta="${f%.jsonl}.meta.json"
      desc=""; atype=""
      if [[ -s "$meta" ]]; then
        desc=$(jq -r '.description // empty' "$meta")
        atype=$(jq -r '.agentType // empty' "$meta")
      fi
      echo; echo "---"; echo
      echo "## Subagent \`$name\`${desc:+: $desc}"
      echo
      echo "Type: \`${atype:-unknown}\` · Source: \`$f\`"
      echo
      jq -c '.' "$f" | render "###"
    done
  fi

  # Subagent transcripts, older layout: sidechain records inside the main file.

# Render a Claude Code JSONL transcript as readable Markdown.
#
# Usage: jq -rs --arg h "##" -f transcript-to-md.jq transcript.jsonl
#   $h  heading prefix for each turn ("##" for the main session, "###" for subagents)
#
# One record per JSONL line. Only user / assistant / non-meta system records are
# rendered; bookkeeping records (attachment, mode, snapshots, ...) are skipped.
# Assistant records arrive one content block per line, so consecutive records
# from the same role are merged under a single heading. Tool results (user
# records that only carry tool_result blocks) are kept inside the assistant turn.

def fence(s):
  ([s | scan("`+") | length] | max // 0) as $m
  | ("`" * ([3, $m + 1] | max)) as $f
  | "\($f)\n\(s)\n\($f)";

def escape_tags:
  gsub("<(?<t>/?system-reminder)>"; "&lt;\(.t)&gt;");

def details(summary; body):
  "<details>\n<summary>\(summary)</summary>\n\n\(body)\n\n</details>";

def ts:
  (.timestamp // "") | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z");

def inline_ok:
  (test("[`\n]") | not) and (length <= 120);

def render_input:
  if type == "object" then
    [ to_entries[]
      | .key as $k | .value as $v
      | if ($v | type) == "string" then
          if ($v | inline_ok) then "- `\($k)`: `\($v)`"
          else "- `\($k)`:\n\n\(fence($v))\n" end
        else "- `\($k)`: `\($v | tojson)`" end
    ] | join("\n")
  else fence(tojson) end;

def result_text:
  .content
  | if type == "string" then .
    elif type == "array" then
      [ .[] | if .type == "text" then .text
              elif .type == "image" then "[image]"
              else tojson end ] | join("\n")
    else (. // "" | tostring) end;

def block:
  if .type == "text" then (.text | escape_tags)
  elif .type == "thinking" then
    if ((.thinking // "") | length) == 0 then empty
    else details("Thinking"; .thinking | escape_tags) end
  elif .type == "tool_use" then
    "**Tool call:** `\(.name)` <sub>\(.id)</sub>\n\n\(.input | render_input)"
  elif .type == "tool_result" then
    ("**Tool result" + (if .is_error == true then " (error)" else "" end)
      + "** <sub>\(.tool_use_id)</sub>") as $s
    | details($s; fence(result_text | escape_tags))
  elif .type == "image" then "[image]"
  else fence(tojson) end;

def is_tool_result_only:
  .type == "user"
  and (.message.content | type) == "array"
  and (.message.content | length) > 0
  and all(.message.content[]; .type == "tool_result");

def role:
  if is_tool_result_only then "assistant" else .type end;

def role_label:
  if .type == "user" then "User"
  elif .type == "assistant" then "Assistant"
  else "System" end;

def heading:
  "\($h) \(role_label) <sub>\(ts)</sub>";

def body:
  if .type == "system" then
    "> **system\(if .subtype then " (\(.subtype))" else "" end):** \((.content // "") | tostring | escape_tags)"
  elif (.message.content | type) == "string" then
    (.message.content | escape_tags)
  else
    [ .message.content[] | block ] | join("\n\n")
  end;

def renderable:
  ((.type == "user" or .type == "assistant") and .message != null)
  or (.type == "system" and .isMeta != true and .content != null);

map(select(renderable))
| reduce .[] as $r ({prev: null, out: []};
    ($r | role) as $role
    | .out += (if $role != .prev then [($r | heading)] else [] end) + ([($r | body)] | map(select(length > 0)))
    | .prev = $role)
| .out
| join("\n\n")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Redeploy parcels.vaz.io: check out a pushed branch on the server, rebuild, restart.
#
#   scripts/deploy.sh            # deploy origin/main
#   scripts/deploy.sh my-branch  # deploy another pushed branch
#
# Server layout (one-time setup, already done):
#   ~e/parcel-rates             git clone of this repo
#   compose.override.yaml       publishes nginx on 127.0.0.1:8090 only (git-excluded)
#   /etc/apache2/sites-available/parcels.vaz.io.conf  proxies https -> 127.0.0.1:8090
# Only pushed commits are deployed; local uncommitted changes are not.
set -euo pipefail

HOST="${DEPLOY_HOST:-e@vaz.io}"
DIR="${DEPLOY_DIR:-parcel-rates}"
BRANCH="${1:-main}"
URL="https://parcels.vaz.io"

echo "==> Deploying origin/$BRANCH to $HOST:~/$DIR"
ssh "$HOST" bash -s -- "$DIR" "$BRANCH" <<'REMOTE'
set -euo pipefail
cd "$HOME/$1"
git fetch --quiet origin
git checkout --quiet --detach "origin/$2"
echo "    at $(git log --oneline -1)"
docker compose up -d --build --remove-orphans
docker image prune -f >/dev/null
REMOTE

echo "==> Checking $URL"
for _ in $(seq 1 20); do
  if curl -fsS "$URL/api/health" >/dev/null 2>&1 && curl -fsS -o /dev/null "$URL/"; then
    echo "    healthy"
    exit 0
  fi
  sleep 3
done
echo "    $URL did not become healthy; check: ssh $HOST 'cd $DIR && docker compose logs --tail=50'" >&2
exit 1
deploy.sh

# Frontend: build the Vite app, then serve it with an unprivileged nginx that
# also proxies /api to the backend service.
FROM node:22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.28-alpine
COPY nginx/default.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
COPY nginx/security-headers.conf nginx/security-headers-base.conf /etc/nginx/snippets/
COPY --from=build /src/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
EXPOSE 8080
server {
    listen 8080;
    server_name _;
    root /usr/share/nginx/html;
    server_tokens off;

    gzip on;
    gzip_vary on;
    gzip_proxied any;
    gzip_min_length 1024;
    gzip_types text/css application/javascript application/json image/svg+xml text/plain;

    # Interactive API docs: Swagger UI is pinned with Subresource Integrity on
    # jsDelivr (backend/app/api/docs.py), so only these two paths allow it.
    location ~ ^/api/docs(/init\.js)?$ {
        include /etc/nginx/snippets/security-headers-base.conf;
        add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net; style-src 'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'" always;
        proxy_pass http://backend:8000;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }

    location /api/ {
        include /etc/nginx/snippets/security-headers.conf;
        proxy_pass http://backend:8000;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_read_timeout 60s;
        client_max_body_size 5m;
    }

    # Hashed build assets never change under the same name.
    location /assets/ {
        include /etc/nginx/snippets/security-headers.conf;
        add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable" always;
        try_files $uri =404;
    }

    # SPA fallback: unknown paths get index.html.
    location / {
        include /etc/nginx/snippets/security-headers.conf;
